definition_zh: 水壶；（烧水用的）壶；一壶的量
definition_en: a metal or plastic container with a handle and a spout, used for boiling water
core_image: 炉架上一只带弯嘴的金属壶，壶嘴正冒着白汽
scene: 清晨厨房里，炉子上的壶刚开始鸣响，窗户蒙上一层雾。 Put the kettle on; we will have tea before we go.
sceneCN: 这里 kettle 是「水壶」（第 1 个义项：烧水用的带柄带嘴容器），句意为把水壶坐上，我们出门前喝杯茶。画面里的物件：厨房、炉子、起雾的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由 kettle 加 -ful 构成，义为「一壶之量」
复合词，指定音鼓，形如倒扣的壶

senses.title: A vessel for boiling water
senses.definition: a container with a lid, handle, and spout, used to boil water
senses.definitionCN: 有盖、柄和壶嘴，用来烧水的容器
senses.example: The kettle began to whistle on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 炉子上的水壶开始呜呜叫。
senses.why: The core object is a vessel built for one job: turning water into steam.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一只专做一件事的容器：把水变成蒸汽。

senses.title: The amount it holds
senses.definition: as much water as such a vessel can hold
senses.definitionCN: 这样一只壶能装下的水量
senses.example: We drank a whole kettle of tea before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午之前我们喝了整整一壶茶。
senses.why: A container easily becomes a unit of measure for what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 容器很容易变成衡量所装之物的单位。

senses.title: A large metal pot for boiling
senses.definition: a large open metal vessel for boiling food or washing, as in older households
senses.definitionCN: 旧时家庭用来煮食物或洗衣的大金属容器
senses.example: The laundry went into the copper kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 要洗的衣服被扔进紫铜大锅。
senses.why: The old large-pot sense survives where the work was done in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 「大锅」这个旧义保留在工作成批进行的地方。

senses.title: A kettle-shaped drum
senses.definition: a drum made of a metal bowl, in the compound kettledrum
senses.definitionCN: 由金属碗状鼓身做成，见复合词 kettledrum
senses.example: The kettledrums opened the march.
senses.exampleCN: 定音鼓为进行曲开场。
senses.why: A drum made of a metal bowl looks exactly like an upturned kettle.
senses.whyCN: 用金属碗做鼓身的鼓，看上去就是倒扣的壶。

senses.title: A group of hawks in flight
senses.definition: a flock of birds of prey circling together on the wind
senses.definitionCN: 指盘旋在气流上的一群猛禽
senses.example: A kettle of hawks rose above the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一群鹰在山脊上空盘旋升起。
senses.why: Birds circling in a rising column suggest something stirring in a pot.
senses.whyCN: 飞鸟在上升气流里盘旋，像锅中翻动的东西。

intro.en: Kettle comes from Old Norse ketill and Latin catillus, a small dish, a word that travelled with the metal itself.
intro.cn: kettle 来自古北欧语 ketill 与拉丁语 catillus「小碟」，这个词是随金属器具一起传播的。

items.en: catillus was a small dish or bowl, from catinus, a deep vessel.
items.cn: catillus 意为小碟或小碗，来自 catinus「深容器」。

items.en: Old Norse ketill named a cauldron, borrowed from Latin-speaking traders.
items.cn: 古北欧语 ketill 指大锅，是从说拉丁语的商人那里借来的。

items.en: Old English cetel and cytel named a cooking pot.
items.cn: 古英语 cetel、cytel 指炊事用锅。

items.en: The form kettle fixed by the Middle English period.
items.cn: kettle 的拼写在中古英语时期固定下来。

items.en: The tea kettle sense dominated once tea became common.
items.cn: 茶普及之后，「烧水壶」义占据主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds vessels and short words close in shape; the near-meaning group holds other water vessels.
note.cn: 形近组收器物与外形相近的词；近义组收其他盛水器具。

entries.definition: Cows and bulls kept on a farm.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一字母，义为「牛群」。

entries.definition: As much as a kettle holds.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kettle 加 -ful 构成，指一壶之量。

entries.definition: Young cats.
entries.definitionCN: 发音相近，义为「小猫」。

entries.definition: A deep round container for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 指较深的锅或罐。

entries.definition: A pot in which tea is made.
entries.definitionCN: 指沏茶的茶壶，通常不上炉。

entries.definition: A large open pot over a fire.
entries.definitionCN: 多用于文学，指火上的大锅。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a Latin small dish to the whistle before tea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「小碟」走到沏茶前的一声鸣响。

normal.en: The same word family gave cauldron through French.
normal.cn: 同一词族经由法语还生出 cauldron。

normal.en: Put the kettle on is a whole offer of tea in four words.
normal.cn: put the kettle on 四个词就等于请人喝茶。

normal.en: An electric kettle switches itself off when it boils.
normal.cn: 电水壶烧开会自动断电。

normal.en: Switching t and c turns kettle into cattle.
normal.cn: 把 t 与 c 一换，kettle 就变 cattle。

normal.en: Kettledrums are named for their bowl shape.
normal.cn: 定音鼓因碗状鼓身得名。

abstract.en: A kettle is a small room built for steam.
abstract.cn: 水壶是为蒸汽造的一间小屋。

abstract.en: The whistle is the sound of patience ending.
abstract.cn: 鸣响是忍耐到头的那个声音。

abstract.en: Every kitchen has one object that announces the morning.
abstract.cn: 每个厨房都有一样东西替早晨开口。

examples.en: She filled the kettle and put it on.
examples.cn: 她把壶灌满坐上了火。

examples.en: The electric kettle boils in under two minutes.
examples.cn: 电水壶不到两分钟就能烧开。

examples.en: He drank a kettle of tea while reading.
examples.cn: 他看书时喝了一整壶茶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开透」—— 水壶里的水，开透了才响

root: 拉丁语 catinus「深容器」→ catillus「小碟」→ 古北欧语 ketill「大锅」→ 古英语 cetel → 中古英语 kettle。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the boiling vessel, its capacity, a large boiling pot, the drum, and a circling flock of hawks.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：烧水壶、一壶之量、大锅、定音鼓，以及盘旋的鹰群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal pot with a bent spout, steaming on the stove.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉上一只弯嘴金属壶正冒着白汽。

branches.en: THE STOVE: the whistle that starts tea.
branches.cn: 炉子这条线：为沏茶开场的那声鸣响。

branches.en: THE CUP LINE: one pot poured out.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：倒空一壶。

branches.en: THE LAUNDRY: a copper pot in the yard.
branches.cn: 洗衣这条线：院子里那口铜锅。

branches.en: THE ORCHESTRA: bowls that keep time.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：打拍子的碗。

branches.en: THE RIDGE: birds circling upward on warm air.
branches.cn: 山脊这条线：顺着暖流盘旋上升的鸟。

intro.en: Kettle is a borrowed noun; English adds only -s and the -ful of quantity.
intro.cn: kettle 是借来的名词，英语只加复数 -s 和表量的 -ful。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives name deep vessels and dishes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都指深容器与小碟。

items.example: The stem survives only in a few words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干只剩在少数词里。
cauldron 保留了更古老的意义。

items.example: It forms put the kettle on.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 put the kettle on。

definition_zh: 拼命的；绝望的；极需的
definition_en: willing to try anything because you feel there is no other way
core_image: 一个人站在崖边，把最后一块木板推出去当作桥
scene: 最后一班车已经开走，他在雨里拦下每一辆经过的车。 The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
sceneCN: 这里 desperate 指「拼命的」（第 1 个义项：因别无出路而不顾一切）；句意是被困的登山者拼命呼救。

senses.title: Ready to risk anything
senses.definition: willing to do something dangerous or extreme because no other choice seems open
senses.definitionCN: 因看不到别的出路而愿意做危险或极端的事
senses.example: The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
senses.exampleCN: 被困的登山者拼命呼救。
senses.why: When every road is closed, one road is chosen without counting the cost.
senses.whyCN: 当所有路都关着，人就会不计代价地选一条。

senses.title: Feeling no hope
senses.definition: feeling that there is no hope and no way out
senses.definitionCN: 觉得没有希望、也没有出路
senses.example: She felt desperate after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次被拒之后，她感到绝望。
senses.why: The feeling and the act sit on the same day: first the dark, then the leap.
senses.whyCN: 感受与行动同处在一天里：先是黑下来，然后纵身一跳。

senses.title: Needing it very badly
senses.definition: needing something very much and having little of it
senses.definitionCN: 非常需要某物而手里几乎没有
senses.example: The team is desperate for a goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队急需一名守门员。
senses.why: A shortage sharpens want until it looks like hunger.
senses.whyCN: 短缺会把想要磨得锋利，直到它看起来像饥饿。

intro.en: Desperate comes from Latin desperatus, the past participle of desperare, to lose hope, from de- plus sperare, to hope.
intro.cn: desperate 来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，由 de- 与 sperare（希望）构成。

items.en: Desperatus described a person or case past all hope.
items.cn: desperatus 形容一个人或一件事已越过所有希望。

items.en: The word was used for the sick, the doomed and the reckless alike.
items.cn: 这个词既用于病人，也用于注定失败的人与不顾一切的人。

items.en: Desesperer gave the adjective its edge of violent effort.
items.cn: desesperer 给了这个形容词一股拼死用力的锋刃。

items.en: English applied it to acts, situations and needs.
items.cn: 英语把它用于行为、处境与需求。

items.en: The everyday sense softened into simply needing something badly.
items.cn: 日常用法又软化成「非常需要某物」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same hope root, and the meaning group moves from no hope to urgent need.
note.cn: 形近组出自同一个表示希望的词根，近义组则从没有希望走到急迫的需要。

entries.definition: the feeling that no hope is left
entries.definitionCN: 毫无希望的感觉

entries.definition: the state of being ready to risk all
entries.definitionCN: 准备孤注一掷的状态

entries.definition: in a hopeless or frantic way
entries.definitionCN: 以绝望或疯狂的方式

entries.definition: having no chance of success
entries.definitionCN: 没有成功机会的

entries.definition: wild with worry or fear
entries.definitionCN: 因担忧或恐惧而狂乱的

entries.definition: needing action right away
entries.definitionCN: 需要立刻行动的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin at the edge of a cliff and end with an empty goal mouth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从悬崖边开始，落到一个空着的球门前。

normal.en: Desperate is what hope looks like when it starts running.
normal.cn: 绝望时的那种拼劲，就是希望开始狂奔的样子。

normal.en: When no road is open, people build one out of boards.
normal.cn: 没有路可走时，人们就用木板搭一条。

normal.en: The word can mean no hope, or simply no goalkeeper.
normal.cn: 这个词可以指毫无希望，也可以只指缺个守门员。

normal.en: De- plus sperare: hope taken away, effort left behind.
normal.cn: de- 加 sperare：希望被拿走，力气留在原地。

normal.en: A desperate measure is a measure taken by someone with no second plan.
normal.cn: 孤注一掷的手段，是没有第二套方案的人用的手段。

abstract.en: Picture a foot testing a plank over a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在试一块横在空隙上的木板。

abstract.en: Picture two hands waving in the rain at a dark road.
abstract.cn: 想象雨中两双手朝一条黑路挥动。

abstract.en: Picture a goal with nobody standing in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有人站着的球门。

examples.en: The stranded climbers made a desperate call for help.
examples.cn: 被困的登山者拼命呼救。

examples.en: She felt desperate after the third rejection.
examples.cn: 第三次被拒之后，她感到绝望。

examples.en: The team is desperate for a goalkeeper.
examples.cn: 这支球队急需一名守门员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desperate 记成「地死怕他」：怕到极点，什么都不顾了，就是拼命。

root: 来自拉丁语 desperatus，是 desperare（失去希望）的过去分词，由 de-（去掉）与 sperare（希望）构成。本义是希望已被耗尽，后来指无路可走时不顾一切的行动，也指心里彻底绝望，再由绝望引申为极度需要。

sensesIntro.en: From a leap taken with no second plan, to the dark feeling behind it, to a shortage that feels like hunger.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有退路时的一跃，到它背后的那片黑，再到像饥饿一样的短缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stepping onto a plank with nothing below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人踏上木板，脚下什么都没有。

branches.en: The first sense is the reckless step itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那不顾一切的一步。

branches.en: The second sense is the darkness that made the step possible.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是让这一步得以发生的那片黑。

branches.en: The third sense is a plain shortage pushing a person forward.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是推着人往前走的单纯短缺。

branches.en: Risk and despair are the outside and inside of one moment.
branches.cn: 冒险与绝望，是同一个瞬间的外面与里面。

branches.en: A team short of a player will try a desperate formation.
branches.cn: 缺一名球员的球队，会试一套拼命的阵型。

intro.en: Desperate shares the hope root with despair and grows forms for manner, state and reckless persons.
intro.cn: desperate 与 despair 共用表示希望的词根，并长出表示方式、状态与亡命之徒的形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope, and de- strips it away; -ate makes the result an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 spes（希望），de- 把它剥走，后缀 -ate 把结果变成形容词。

items.example: She tried desperately to hold on.

items.meaning: the state of having no hope
items.example: In desperation he sold the car.
items.exampleCN: 走投无路之下他卖掉了车。

items.example: There was a strange desperateness in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 他的声音里有一种奇怪的不顾一切。

items.example: The desperado rode off at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 那个亡命之徒天亮时骑马走了。
她发出一声绝望的叫喊。

definition_zh: 阐明；说明；演示；给（书）加插图
definition_en: to make something clear by giving examples or pictures, or to add pictures to a book
core_image: 黑板上被老师用红粉笔圈出的一幅示意图
scene: 物理老师讲浮力时先放下教材，转身在黑板上画了一条船。 She used two arrows to illustrate how the water pushed the hull upward.
sceneCN: 这里 illustrate 是「阐明、说明」（第 1 个义项：用例子或图示把道理讲清），句意是她用两个箭头说明水如何把船体托起。画面里有黑板、红粉笔和一艘简笔画的船。

pos.zh: 动词：阐明、说明；给书加插图

senses.title: To make an idea clear
senses.definition: to explain something by giving examples or by showing how it works
senses.definitionCN: 用例子或演示来说明某事
senses.example: Let me illustrate the rule with a simple case.
senses.exampleCN: 让我用个简单的例子说明这条规则。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to light up, and an example does exactly that for an abstract idea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根本是「照亮」，而例子对抽象观念所做的正是照亮。

senses.title: To add pictures to a text
senses.definition: to supply drawings or photographs for a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 为书籍或杂志提供插图或照片
senses.example: A young artist illustrated the whole storybook.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻画家为整本故事书画了插图。
senses.why: Pictures make a text bright and easy to grasp, so the same verb was extended from words to images.
senses.whyCN: 图画使文字明朗易懂，于是同一个动词从说明扩展到配图。

senses.title: To be an example of
senses.definition: to serve as a clear instance that shows a general fact
senses.definitionCN: 作为能说明普遍事实的明确例子
senses.example: His career illustrates how talent and luck combine.
senses.exampleCN: 他的经历说明了天赋与运气如何结合。
senses.why: When a case makes a truth visible, English lets the case itself become the subject and light up the claim.
senses.whyCN: 当一个事例让道理显现时，英语就让这个事例作主语，替主张打光。

intro.en: Illustrate goes back to a Latin verb for lighting up, and that image of light still sits inside the word.
intro.cn: illustrate 可追溯到一个意为「照亮」的拉丁动词，光的意象至今留在词里。

items.en: Lustrare meant to light up or make bright, and was used of light striking a dark place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lustrare 意为照亮、使明亮，常指光照进暗处。

items.en: Illustrare strengthened it: to throw light on, and figuratively to make clear to the mind.
items.cn: illustrare 加强此义：把光照上去，引申为使心中明白。

items.en: Church writers used illustrare of famous men whose deeds lit up their age.
items.cn: 教会作家用 illustrare 形容功业照亮时代的著名人物。

items.en: English borrowed it as illustren, first meaning to enlighten or bring honour.
items.cn: 英语以 illustren 借入，最初意为启迪或增光。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the printing trade made to add pictures the everyday meaning.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，印刷业让「加插图」成了最日常的词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for making things clear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁家族里的词；近义组收其他表示讲清楚的动词。

entries.definition: A picture or example that lights up a point.
entries.definitionCN: 插图或例证，用来把观点照亮。

entries.definition: Famous and admired, literally shining with light.
entries.definitionCN: 著名的、辉煌的，字面就是「发光」。

entries.definition: A soft shine on a surface, from the same light word.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的柔和光泽，同出光明一词。

entries.definition: To make something plain by giving reasons; broader than illustrate.
entries.definitionCN: 通过讲道理把事情说清楚，范围比 illustrate 更广。

entries.definition: To show clearly by doing or by proof.
entries.definitionCN: 通过演示或证据明确展示。

entries.definition: To remove confusion from a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 消除说法中的含混之处。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the light inside illustrare to pictures, examples and clear blackboard arrows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 illustrare 里的「光」连到插图、例子与黑板上清晰的箭头。

normal.en: The Latin root means light: to illustrate is to shine a lamp on an idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为光：illustrate 就是给一个想法打灯。

normal.en: The ill- here is not a negative prefix, so do not read it as not legal.
normal.cn: 这里的 ill- 不是否定前缀，别误读成「不合法」。

normal.en: The stress falls in the middle: il-LUS-trate.
normal.cn: 重音在中间：il-LUS-trate。

normal.en: -ate marks a verb, and its relatives are all nouns or adjectives of light and picture.
normal.cn: -ate 标示动词，它的同族词都与光和图画相关。

normal.en: A book with pictures is an illustrated book, so the verb keeps a footprint on every page.
normal.cn: 带图的书叫 illustrated book，这个动词在每一页上都留下脚印。

abstract.en: Explaining and drawing are two limbs of one act: both pull an invisible thought into the visible world.
abstract.cn: 讲解与绘图是同一动作的两条胳膊：都把看不见的想法拉进可见世界。

abstract.en: The word trusts the example more than the rule, because a lit case teaches faster than a definition.
abstract.cn: 这个词更信例子而非规则，因为被照亮的事例比定义教得快。

abstract.en: A single illustration can do what a whole paragraph cannot, which is why the picture stayed inside the verb.
abstract.cn: 一幅插图能做出整段文字做不到的事，所以图画一直住在动词里。

examples.en: The teacher illustrated the idea with a simple diagram.
examples.cn: 老师用一张简图说明了这个概念。

examples.en: This case clearly illustrates why the rules are needed.
examples.cn: 这个案例清楚说明了为什么需要这些规则。

examples.en: She has illustrated more than thirty children's books.
examples.cn: 她为三十多本童书绘制过插图。

dict_mnemonic.text: illustr 光（拉丁语「照亮」）+ ate 动词——把光照到想法上，就是阐明；配图也是照亮

root: 拉丁语 lustrare「照亮」→ illustrare「照亮、使明白」，中世纪拉丁语引申为增光，中古英语借入为 illustren，近代定形 illustrate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: to make an idea clear, to add pictures to a text, and to serve as a telling example.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：讲清一个观点、给文字配图，以及本身成为有力的例证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red chalk circle on a blackboard diagram, lighting up how a boat floats.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板示意图上被红粉笔圈出的一处，照亮船为什么浮。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM LINE: an example illuminates an abstract rule.
branches.cn: 课堂线：一个例子照亮一条抽象规则。

branches.en: THE PRINT LINE: drawings light up a page of text.
branches.cn: 印刷线：图画照亮一整页文字。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE LINE: a career or a case can be the example itself.
branches.cn: 证据线：一段经历或一个案例本身就充当例证。

branches.en: THE LIGHT LINE: all three keep the original image of throwing light.
branches.cn: 光之线：三个义项都保留「投光」的原意象。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: in essays the verb introduces proof, not decoration.
branches.cn: 论证线：在议论文里这个词引出的是证据，不是装饰。

intro.en: Illustrate is a Latin verb taken over almost whole, with English endings and a large family of relatives.
intro.cn: illustrate 几乎是整体搬来的拉丁动词，只换英语词尾，并带出一大串同族词。

latinIntro.en: The light root lustr- is recorded in Latin, and the prefix il- here is the preposition in-, not a negative.
latinIntro.cn: 表示光的词根 lustr- 有拉丁文献，这里的前缀 il- 是介词 in- 的变形，并非否定。

items.example: The root also hides in lustre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也藏在 lustre 里。

items.example: Create and activate behave the same way.
items.exampleCN: create 与 activate 也一样。
她的经历说明了这种危险。

items.meaning: past form or describing a book with pictures
items.meaningCN: 过去式，或形容配有插图的书

items.exampleCN: 这些数字只是示意性的。

items.example: The illustrator signed the first page.
items.exampleCN: 插画家在第一页签了名。

latinEntries.meaning: to light up, to make bright

definition_zh: 成套工具；工具箱；配套元件；装备
definition_en: a set of parts or tools kept together for a particular purpose, or the equipment a person carries for an activity
core_image: 一只敞开的帆布箱，工具、零件与说明按格摆齐
scene: 车停在山路边熄了火，后备箱里那只帆布包派上了用场。 He opened the repair kit and found a spare belt and a small torch in it.
sceneCN: 这里 kit 是「成套工具、工具箱」（第 1 个义项：为某用途配套收纳的一套工具或零件），句意是他打开修理包，在里面找到一条备用皮带和一只小手电。画面里有山路、熄火的车和敞开的帆布包。

pos.zh: 名词：成套工具；配套元件；装备
动词：装备（用 kit out、kit up 搭配）

derivatives.zh: kit 的复数形式，义为「多套工具或装备」
由动词加 -ed 构成，英式口语义为「装备齐全的」
kit 与 bag 合成，义为「行囊、工具袋」
外形相近但词源不同，义为「厨房」

senses.title: A set of tools kept together
senses.definition: a set of tools, parts, or equipment packed together for a specific job
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途配套收纳的工具、零件或装备
senses.example: Every car should carry a basic tool kit.
senses.exampleCN: 每辆车都该带一套基本工具。
senses.why: The word started as a wooden tub for holding a soldier things, and the container came to stand for the set it held.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指装士兵杂物的木盆，容器后来代表它所装的那一整套。

senses.title: Equipment for an activity
senses.definition: the clothes and equipment that a person needs for a sport, a job, or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 个人从事运动、工作或旅行所需的衣物与器具
senses.example: His football kit was drying on the radiator.
senses.exampleCN: 他的足球装备正在暖气片上晾着。
senses.why: Once it named a soldier belongings, the word naturally widened to anyone gear for a task.
senses.whyCN: 它既曾指士兵的随身之物，扩而广之指任何人做某件事的行头。

senses.title: Parts sold ready to assemble
senses.definition: a set of parts sold together to be put together by the buyer, as for a model or furniture
senses.definitionCN: 一起出售、由购买者自行组装的零件，如模型或家具
senses.example: The shelf came as a kit with screws and a diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 这个架子以套件形式出售，附螺丝和图解。
senses.why: In trade the container word turned into a commercial unit: everything you need, sold in one box.
senses.whyCN: 在买卖里，容器词变成了一个出售单位：所需之物全装在一只箱子里卖出。

senses.title: To equip someone
senses.definition: in the phrases kit out and kit up, to provide someone with clothes or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于 kit out、kit up，指为某人提供衣物或装备
senses.example: The team was kitted out in new shirts.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍换上了整套新球衣。
senses.why: From the noun of supplies came the verb of handing them out, a frequent path in English.
senses.whyCN: 由补给品之名的名词生出「发放补给」的动词，这是英语里常见的一条路。

intro.en: Kit appears in late Middle English as the name of a wooden tub, and the history before that is debated.
intro.cn: kit 在中古英语晚期以「木盆」之义出现，再往前的来历尚有争议。

items.en: Kyt or kit named a wooden tub or tankard used for holding liquids or provisions.
items.cn: kyt 或 kit 指盛液体或食物的木盆、木桶。

items.en: The closest early relative is the Middle Dutch kitte, a wooden tub made of staves, which supports a Dutch source.
items.cn: 最早的近亲是中古荷兰语 kitte，一种板条拼成的木盆，这支持荷兰语来源说。

items.en: A link with German Kütze or with Old French cuve has also been proposed, and scholars do not fully agree.
items.cn: 也有人提出与德语 Kütze 或古法语 cuve 有关，学界尚未取得一致。

items.en: Soldiers carried a kit, and from the tub the name shifted to the whole set of personal gear.
items.cn: 士兵随身带着 kit，名字由木盆转到了整套个人装备上。

items.en: In the twentieth century kit became the standard word for a boxed set of parts, from models to medical supplies.
items.cn: 二十世纪里 kit 成为「盒装成套零件」的标准说法，从模型到医疗用品都用它。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ from kit by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a prepared set.
note.cn: 形近组收与 kit 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「备好的一套」的说法。

entries.definition: One letter apart; it names the flying toy and a bird of prey.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指风筝以及一种猛禽。

entries.definition: Adds a syllable to kit and names a young cat.
entries.definitionCN: 在 kit 后多加一个音节，指小猫。

entries.definition: Differs by one letter and means a young goat or, informally, a child.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指小山羊，口语中也指孩子。

entries.definition: A group of things used together, wider and more neutral than kit.
entries.definitionCN: 一起使用的一组物品，范围更宽、语体更中性。

entries.definition: A container of goods sold or carried together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起出售或携带的一包物品。

entries.definition: Equipment for an activity, usually uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 某项活动所用的装备，通常不可数。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the wooden tub, the soldier bag and the modern boxed set that the word has named in turn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把木盆、士兵行囊与现代盒装套件依次连起来，这几个东西都曾被这个词指称。

normal.en: Kit doubles the t before -ed and -ing: kitted, kitting.
normal.cn: kit 在加 -ed、-ing 前要双写 t：kitted、kitting。

normal.en: The word once meant a wooden tub; the container still leads to the contents.
normal.cn: 这个词曾指木盆；容器仍然指向它所装的东西。

normal.en: First-aid kit and tool kit are the two phrases you will meet most.
normal.cn: first-aid kit 与 tool kit 是最常遇到的两个搭配。

normal.en: Kit out is the verb form: to fit someone out with gear.
normal.cn: kit out 是动词用法：给某人配齐装备。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with kitchen, which is only a look-alike, not a relative.
normal.cn: 别与厨房 kitchen 混淆，后者只是形近，并非同源。

abstract.en: A kit is a promise of readiness: everything has its place before the need arrives.
abstract.cn: 一套 kit 就是一份「已准备好」的承诺：在需要到来之前，一切各就各位。

abstract.en: The word moves from the box to what is in it, the way a toolbox can stand for the tools.
abstract.cn: 这个词从箱子走到箱中之物，正如工具箱可以代表工具本身。

abstract.en: Parts in a kit are potential: they become a shelf or a model only when someone puts them together.
abstract.cn: 套件里的零件只是潜能：有人把它们拼起来，才成为架子或模型。

examples.en: Take a first-aid kit on the hike.
examples.cn: 徒步时带上一只急救箱。

examples.en: The model plane came as a kit for beginners.
examples.cn: 这架模型飞机以适合初学者的套件形式出售。

examples.en: The club kitted out the new players in matching shirts.
examples.cn: 俱乐部给新队员配齐了统一球衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「齐特」——齐全的特殊物件，装成一箱就是成套工具

root: 中古英语 kyt / kit 指木盆、木桶，可能来自中古荷兰语 kitte（板条木盆），也有德语或古法语来源的猜测，尚无定论；后指士兵的随身行囊，再引申为「一整套工具、装备、套件」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the set of tools in a container, a person own equipment, a boxed set of parts to assemble, and the verb of equipping.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：装在容器里的一套工具，个人装备，盒装配件，以及「给某人配装备」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open canvas box with every tool and part in its own slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只敞开的帆布箱，工具与零件各在各自的格子里。

branches.en: THE TOOLS: the set is kept together so that a job can be done at once.
branches.cn: 工具线：整套放在一起，随时可以动手。

branches.en: THE PERSON: gear for a sport or journey belongs to one body.
branches.cn: 个人线：运动或旅行的装备归属于一个人。

branches.en: THE BOX SALE: parts sold together, to be built at home.
branches.cn: 盒装线：零件一起出售，由买者在家里装好。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the noun of supplies gives a verb of handing them out.
branches.cn: 动词线：补给品之名生出「发放补给」的动词。

branches.en: THE OLD TUB: the container image still explains why a kit holds a set.
branches.cn: 旧木盆线：容器的意象仍能解释为什么 kit 装着一整套。

intro.en: Kit is a short native noun that grows by inflection and by compounds rather than by Latin affixes.
intro.cn: kit 是短小的本土名词，靠词形变化与合成扩展，而非拉丁语词缀。

latinIntro.en: Kit has no Latin source; the tub words below are given only as historical neighbours.
latinIntro.cn: kit 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些「桶、盆」词只作为历史上的近邻列出。

items.meaning: a set of tools or gear

items.example: Both kits are on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 两个工具箱都在架子上。

items.example: The team is kitted and ready.
items.exampleCN: 队伍装备齐整，准备就绪。

items.example: Kitting out a new lab takes weeks.
items.exampleCN: 给新实验室配齐装备要花好几周。

items.meaningCN: 与 kit 构成 kit out
items.exampleCN: 它补足 kit out 这一搭配。

items.meaningCN: 与 kit 构成 kit up
items.exampleCN: 它补足 kit up 这一搭配。

items.example: He threw his kitbag on the bus.
items.exampleCN: 他把行李袋扔上了巴士。
它把 kit 变成 kits。

latinEntries.structure: Medieval Latin noun from Latin cupa

definition_zh: 经销商；商人；发牌者
definition_en: a person or business that buys and sells goods, or one who gives out cards
core_image: 车行里挂着钥匙、笑着迎人的销售员
scene: 车行老板把钥匙放在柜台上，报了一个价。 The dealer offered a lower price.
sceneCN: 这里 dealer 指「经销商」（第 1 个义项：买卖某类商品的人或商号）；句意是经销商报了一个更低的价。

senses.title: A person who trades
senses.definition: someone whose business is buying and selling a kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 以买卖某类商品为业的人
senses.example: The dealer offered a lower price.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商报了一个更低的价。
senses.why: The suffix -er turns the act of dealing into a person who lives by it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把「做买卖」这个动作，变成靠它生活的人。

senses.title: The one who gives out cards
senses.definition: the person who shares the cards among the players
senses.definitionCN: 在玩牌的人之间分牌的人
senses.example: The dealer turned over the first card.
senses.exampleCN: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。
senses.why: The oldest sense of dealing is feeding cards to the table.
senses.whyCN: dealing 最老的意思，就是给牌桌递牌。

intro.en: Dealer is deal plus -er, so it names whoever divides or hands out.
intro.cn: dealer 是 deal 加 -er 构成，指负责分配或递出东西的人。

items.en: The base verb meant to divide among people.
items.cn: 词根动词意为在众人之间分配。

items.en: A dealer was simply one who handed out shares.
items.cn: dealer 最初只指分份的人。

items.en: Card players gave the word its lasting use at the table.
items.cn: 打牌的人让这个词在牌桌上固定下来。

items.en: Dealer also named a merchant of one particular goods.
items.cn: dealer 也开始指经营某一类商品的商人。

items.en: Car dealer, art dealer, and drug dealer fixed the pattern.
items.cn: car dealer、art dealer 与 drug dealer 固定了这一模式。

note.en: The look-alike group ends in -aler, and the meaning group names others who move goods.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -aler 结尾，近义组则列出其他转手货物的人。

entries.definition: to divide or do business
entries.definitionCN: 分配或做生意

entries.definition: a person who makes others well
entries.definitionCN: 使他人痊愈的人

entries.definition: a person who guides a group
entries.definitionCN: 带领一群人的人

entries.definition: a person who trades in goods on a large scale
entries.definitionCN: 大规模做货物买卖的人

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells for a living
entries.definitionCN: 以买卖为生的人

entries.definition: a firm that provides goods to others
entries.definitionCN: 向他人供货的公司

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand of cards spread on a table and end with a row of cars under bright lights.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从摊在桌上的一手牌开始，落到灯下一排亮闪闪的车。

normal.en: A dealer is the one who decides how the shares fall.
normal.cn: 经销商是决定份额怎么落下的人。

normal.en: The card table gave the word its first steady job.
normal.cn: 牌桌给了这个词第一份稳定的工作。

normal.en: Add -er to dealing and you have put a person in the shop.
normal.cn: 给 dealing 加 -er，店里就多了一个人。

normal.en: A good dealer knows the goods better than the buyer does.
normal.cn: 好商人比买家更懂自己的货。

normal.en: The word carries no judgement; the goods decide that.
normal.cn: 这个词本身不带评判，是货物在决定评判。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of cards sliding across green cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一把牌滑过绿绒桌面。

abstract.en: Picture keys hanging in rows behind a glass counter.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜台后一排排挂着的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture two men talking quietly beside a parked car.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在一辆停着的车旁低声交谈。

examples.en: The dealer offered a lower price.
examples.cn: 经销商报了一个更低的价。

examples.en: The dealer turned over the first card.
examples.cn: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。

examples.en: They bought the van from a local dealer.
examples.cn: 他们从本地经销商那里买了那辆面包车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dealer 记成「递了」：deal 是分，-er 是人，把货一件件递出去的人就是经销商。

root: 由 deal（分配、交易）加施动后缀 -er 构成；中古英语时指分份的人，十六世纪因纸牌而固定为「发牌者」，十七世纪起又指经营某一类商品的商人。

sensesIntro.en: From the hand that shares out cards, to the shop that shares out goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分牌的那只手，到分发货物的那家店。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a share of something across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一份东西推过柜台。

branches.en: The first sense is a person whose living is the exchange itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是以交换本身为生的人。

branches.en: The second is the same hand, sharing cards instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个是同一只手，分的是牌而不是货。

branches.en: Both senses depend on giving each person a fair share.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠给每个人一份公道。

branches.en: The card table is the older picture under the shop.
branches.cn: 牌桌是商店底下那幅更老的画。

branches.en: A dealer never keeps the whole deck.
branches.cn: 经销商从不把整副牌都留下。

intro.en: Dealer is a person noun built on deal, and its compounds are named by the goods it handles.
intro.cn: dealer 是建在 deal 上的人称名词，复合词则按经手的货物来命名。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; deal is native Germanic and -er is a Germanic agent ending.
latinIntro.cn: 不涉及拉丁词根：deal 是本族日耳曼词，-er 也是日耳曼语的施动后缀。

items.meaning: one who trades or gives out
items.exampleCN: 这位经销商熟悉每一款车。

items.meaning: a shop licensed to sell a brand
items.example: The dealership is on the ring road.
The car dealer gave a warranty.

items.meaning: a trader in paintings and sculpture
items.example: An art dealer bought the sketch.
items.exampleCN: 一位艺术品商买下了那张草图。

items.meaning: the person who gives out cards
items.example: The card dealer smiled and shuffled.
items.exampleCN: 发牌的人笑了笑，开始洗牌。

items.meaning: a person who sells illegal drugs
items.example: The police caught the drug dealer.
items.exampleCN: 警方抓住了那个毒品贩子。

definition_zh: 整洁的；整齐的；可观的；（使）整洁；收拾
definition_en: arranged neatly and in order, or to make a place neat and ordered
core_image: 归位的抽屉：每样东西都回到自己的格子里
scene: 客人快到了，她赶紧收拾客厅。 She tidied the living room before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 tidy 是「收拾、整理」（第 4 个义项：使整洁）；句意：客人到之前她整理了客厅。

pos.zh: 整洁的；整齐的；相当大的

derivatives.zh: tidy 加 -ly，义为「整洁地；整齐地」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不整洁的；凌乱的」

senses.title: Neat and in good order
senses.definition: arranged with everything in its proper place, with nothing out of order
senses.definitionCN: 一切安排妥当、各归其位，毫无杂乱
senses.example: Her desk is always tidy.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书桌总是很整洁。
senses.why: The core image is the drawer where every object sits in its slot; nothing strays.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是每样东西都待在自己格子里的抽屉；无一游离。

senses.title: Orderly in habits or appearance
senses.definition: showing a habit of keeping things, or oneself, neat and ordered
senses.definitionCN: 表现出保持物品或自身整洁的习惯
senses.example: He is very tidy about his paperwork.
senses.exampleCN: 他整理文件井井有条。
senses.why: If a space can be tidy, the person who keeps it that way takes the word too.
senses.whyCN: 空间可整洁，维持空间的人也顺理成章戴上这顶帽子。

senses.title: A considerable amount
senses.definition: used to describe an amount of money that is pleasantly large
senses.definitionCN: 形容一笔令人满意的巨款
senses.example: She earns a tidy sum from her investments.
senses.exampleCN: 她从投资中赚得一笔可观的钱。
senses.why: A neat pile of money is well stacked and large, like a tidy room well arranged.
senses.whyCN: 码得整齐的一堆钱，如整洁的房间般排布讲究且数量可观。

senses.title: To make a place neat
senses.definition: to put things back in order so that a place becomes neat
senses.definitionCN: 把东西归置整齐，使地方恢复井然
senses.example: The children tidied their bedrooms.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们收拾了自己的卧室。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a verb: to give a room the quality of being tidy.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动词：赋予房间「整洁」这一品质。

senses.title: To tidy up: finish small remaining tasks
senses.definition: to deal with the small loose ends that remain at the end of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 处理活动结束后遗留的零星事项
senses.example: Let me tidy up a few details before we publish.
senses.exampleCN: 发布前让我把几个细节收尾。
senses.why: Sweeping the last odds and ends into place completes the ordered picture.
senses.whyCN: 把最后的零碎归位，画面才算完整有序。

senses.title: To tidy away: remove after use
senses.definition: to take away things that have been used and put them where they belong
senses.definitionCN: 把用过的东西拿走并放回原处
senses.example: She tidied away the toys after playtime.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏时间结束后她把玩具收了起来。
senses.why: Restoring each object to its slot is the same motion that keeps a room tidy.
senses.whyCN: 把每件物品送回格子，正是维持整洁的同一个动作。

senses.title: Tidy in result: clean and effective
senses.definition: done neatly and efficiently, without waste or confusion
senses.definitionCN: 做得干净利落、不浪费不含混
senses.example: He gave a tidy account of the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个方案讲得条理分明。
senses.why: Order in space becomes order in thought and action.
senses.whyCN: 空间之序转化为思路与行动之序。

senses.title: A tidy profit or gain
senses.definition: a profit that is satisfyingly large, often after simple effort
senses.definitionCN: 令人满意的大额利润，常指付出不大却收获颇丰
senses.example: They made a tidy profit on the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 那套公寓让他们赚了笔可观的利润。
senses.why: Money stacked as neatly as a tidy room suggests both order and abundance.
senses.whyCN: 钱像整洁的房间一样码放整齐，兼有秩序与充裕之意。

intro.en: Tidy comes from the Old English tide, meaning time or season, plus -y. A tidy state was originally timely, happening at the right moment; order and the right time were once one idea.
intro.cn: tidy 源自古英语 tide「时间、时节」加 -y。tidy 的本义是「适时的、合于时宜的」；秩序与合时原本是同一个概念。

items.en: Tid meant a time or season, the root behind tidings and eventide.
items.cn: 古英语 tid 意为时间、季节，是 tidings、eventide 的词根。

items.en: Tidi meant timely, in good season, done at the proper moment.
items.cn: 中古英语 tidi 意为适时、合于时节。

items.en: The sense shifted to neat and well arranged, as if order kept everything in its right time and place.
items.cn: 词义转为整齐有序，仿佛秩序让万物各得其所、各逢其时。

items.en: The verb to tidy and the sense of a considerable sum appeared.
items.cn: 动词 to tidy 与「可观款项」义在此期出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps tidy for neatness, for sizeable amounts, and for cleaning up.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tidy 兼指整洁、可观数额与收拾整理。

note.en: The first group gathers the time-root family; the second lists near neighbours in neatness.
note.cn: 第一组是「时间」词根家族；第二组列出整洁义上的近邻。

entries.definition: news, from the same old word for time or season
entries.definitionCN: 消息、音讯，与 tidy 同出「时」根

entries.definition: the close of day, evening, built on the same tide root
entries.definitionCN: 黄昏、日暮，同样建立在 tide 词根上

entries.definition: liking order in thought as well as in things
entries.definitionCN: 思想与事物皆求条理的

entries.definition: clean and precisely arranged, often with a hint of skill
entries.definitionCN: 干净且安排精确，常含巧妙之意

entries.definition: arranged according to a system or rule
entries.definitionCN: 依系统或规则排列的

entries.definition: free of unnecessary objects or detail
entries.definitionCN: 无多余杂物或细节的

normalIntro.en: Real links: tidy from time, tidy up, a tidy sum, and the tidy family of tidings and eventide.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tidy 源于「时间」、tidy up、a tidy sum、以及 tidings 与 eventide 的同根家族。

normal.en: Tidy grew from tide: things in order arrive at their right time and place.
normal.cn: tidy 由 tide 生长而来：有序之物各逢其时、各归其位。

normal.en: Tidy up covers both rooms and loose ends of work.
normal.cn: tidy up 既指收拾房间，也指收尾零星工作。

normal.en: A tidy sum is money stacked as neatly as a tidy drawer.
normal.cn: a tidy sum 是码得像整洁抽屉一般的钱。

normal.en: Untidy simply adds the no-prefix to undo the order.
normal.cn: untidy 只是加上否定前缀，把秩序撤掉。

normal.en: Tidings and eventide keep the original time meaning alive.
normal.cn: tidings 与 eventide 保留了原本的「时间」义。

abstract.en: Order is time made visible: each thing in the moment and place it belongs.
abstract.cn: 秩序是可见的时间：每样东西在属于它的时刻与位置。

abstract.en: A tidy space quiets the mind that lives in it.
abstract.cn: 整洁的空间安抚栖居其中的头脑。

abstract.en: Putting things back is a small promise kept to your future self.
abstract.cn: 物归原处是对未来的自己许下并兑现的小承诺。

examples.en: Keep your workspace tidy to think clearly.
examples.cn: 保持工作区整洁有助于清晰思考。

examples.en: The twins tidied the kitchen in ten minutes.
examples.cn: 双胞胎十分钟就把厨房收拾好了。

examples.en: The sale brought in a tidy sum.
examples.cn: 这次甩卖进账可观。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬地」——把东西从地上抬起来放回原处，屋子立刻 tidy 整洁 → tidy 整洁；收拾

root: 古英语 tīd「时间、时节」+ 形容词后缀 -y → 「适时的」→「整齐有序的」；与 tidings「消息」、eventide「黄昏」同源，核心是「各逢其时、各归其位」。

sensesIntro.en: Timely order becomes neat spaces, neat habits, neatly stacked sums, and finally verbs for restoring order.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「适时之序」生出整洁的空间、整洁的习惯、码放齐整的钱款，最终动词化为恢复秩序的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every object resting in its own slot at its own moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：每样东西在自己的时刻安坐于自己的格子。

branches.en: Order visible in the space around you.
branches.cn: 秩序显形于周遭空间。

branches.en: The habit of keeping order becomes a trait.
branches.cn: 维持秩序的习惯沉淀为品性。

branches.en: Neatly stacked money reads as abundance.
branches.cn: 码放齐整的钱读作丰裕。

branches.en: The verb returns things to their slots.
branches.cn: 动词把东西送回格子。

branches.en: Order extends to loose ends and clear accounts.
branches.cn: 秩序延伸到收尾与条理分明的陈述。

intro.en: Tidy is Germanic; its items show the -y adjective ending and the tidy verb phrases.
intro.cn: tidy 属日耳曼语源；词条展示 -y 形容词词尾与 tidy 动词短语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates exist; the related Germanic formations are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁同源词；下表列出相关日耳曼构词。

items.meaning: to make a place neat; to finish loose ends
to remove and store after use

items.example: The tidiness of the lab impressed visitors.
items.exampleCN: 实验室的整洁令访客印象深刻。

items.example: An untidy heap of clothes lay on the chair.

definition_zh: 时刻；场合；重大活动；时机；机会；理由；原因
definition_en: a particular time when something happens; also a special event, an opportunity, and a reason or cause
core_image: 一枚怀表停在某个刻度上，指针正好落在值得记下的那一格
scene: 老钟表匠把怀表擦得发亮，说这块表只在最要紧的日子才舍得戴。 He wore the old watch only on a special occasion, when the family gathered.
sceneCN: 这里是「场合、重大活动」（第 2 个义项：人们特意参加的重要活动）；句意为他只在全家团聚的特殊场合才戴上那块旧表。可辨物件：怀表、擦表布、老钟表匠手中的放大镜。

derivatives.zh: 由 occasion 加 -al 构成，义为「偶尔的；时不时的」
由 occasional 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶尔；有时」
由动词 occasion 加 -ed 构成，义为「由……引起的」

senses.title: A particular time when something happens
senses.definition: a particular point or moment in time at which something happens
senses.definitionCN: 事情发生的某一个具体时点
senses.example: On that occasion she arrived an hour late.
senses.exampleCN: 那一次她晚到了一个小时。
senses.why: Latin occasio named the moment that falls to a person, from a verb for falling, so the oldest layer is simply a point in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occasio 指落在某人身上的那个时刻，源头是表示「落下」的动词；所以这个词最古老的一层就是时间上的某一点。

senses.title: A special event or ceremony
senses.definition: an important event, ceremony or celebration that people attend
senses.definitionCN: 人们特意前往参加的重要活动、典礼或庆典
senses.example: The wedding was a grand occasion for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是全村的一件盛事。
senses.why: A moment that people mark, dress up for and gather around stops being mere clock time and becomes the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 当某个时刻被人们特意标注、盛装赶去相聚，它就不再只是钟表上的一点，而成了事件本身。

senses.title: A chance to do something
senses.definition: an opportunity or suitable moment for doing something
senses.definitionCN: 适合去做某事的时机或机会
senses.example: She took the occasion to thank everyone who had helped her.
senses.exampleCN: 她借这个机会感谢了所有帮助过她的人。
senses.why: If time can fall favourably into your hands, then that favourable fall is exactly an opening, which is why occasion also means opportunity.
senses.whyCN: 如果时间可以恰好落进你手里，那么这次有利的「落下」本身就是一道开口；所以 occasion 又能表示时机与机会。

senses.title: A reason or cause for something
senses.definition: a reason or ground for doing something, or a cause of an event
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的理由、依据，或某件事的起因
senses.example: There is no occasion for alarm; the test is only a rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 没有理由惊慌，这不过是一次演练。
senses.why: Latin occasio also carried the sense of ground or cause, and English kept it in phrases that ask whether there is any occasion for worry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occasio 还带着「依据、缘由」的意思，英语把它保留在问「有没有理由担心」这类说法里。

intro.en: Occasion is built on a Latin verb for falling: the word first named the moment that falls to a person, then the event, the chance and the reason.
intro.cn: occasion 建立在一个表示「落下」的拉丁动词上：这个词先指落到某人头上的时刻，再指事件、机会与理由。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it is the root behind case, accident and cadence as well.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下，也是 case、accident 与 cadence 的共同词根。

items.en: Ob- plus cadere made occidere, to fall down or fall upon, and also to happen or befall.
items.cn: ob- 与 cadere 合成 occidere，意为倒下、落到……上，也指发生、降临。

items.en: Occasio named the falling moment, the right time or opportunity, and also the ground or cause of an event.
items.cn: occasio 指落下的那一刻，即合适的时机、机会，也指事情的依据或原因。

items.en: Old French occasion carried the same set of meanings: time, opportunity and cause.
items.cn: 古法语 occasion 带着同一组意思：时刻、机会与原因。

items.en: Modern English keeps the time sense, extends it to important events, and still uses the word for a reason.
items.cn: 现代英语保留时间义，把它扩展到重要活动，也仍然用这个词表示理由。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin verb for falling; the near-meaning group collects words for moments, events and chances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「落下」之上的同族词，近义组收表示时刻、事件与机会的词。

entries.definition: Happening from time to time, not regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 不时发生的，并非定期。

entries.definition: Sometimes, but not often.
entries.definitionCN: 有时，但不常。

entries.definition: An unexpected event that causes damage.
entries.definitionCN: 造成损害的意外事件。

entries.definition: A rhythm of rising and falling sound.
entries.definitionCN: 声音起落的节奏。

entries.definition: A very short period of time, or a particular point in it.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，或其中的某一时点。

entries.definition: A situation that makes it possible to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为可能的境况。

entries.definition: Something important that happens.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的重要事情。

entries.definition: A cause or explanation for something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的起因或解释。

normalIntro.en: The word falls out of the Latin verb cadere, and a moment that falls toward you becomes a time, an event, a chance and a reason.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁动词 cadere（落下）里长出来，而一个朝你落下的时刻，会变成时间、事件、机会与理由。

normal.en: Occasion rests on cadere, the Latin verb to fall, and means a moment that falls to you.
normal.cn: occasion 立在拉丁动词 cadere（落下）之上，指落到你头上的那个时刻。

normal.en: Occidere, to fall down, also meant to happen, which is why an occasion can be an event.
normal.cn: occidere 意为倒下，也指发生，所以 occasion 可以指一件事件。

normal.en: A moment that falls favourably becomes an opportunity, the third sense of the word.
normal.cn: 有利落下的时刻就成了机会，也就是这个词的第三个义项。

normal.en: The same Latin noun also meant ground or cause, so occasion can name a reason.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁名词也指依据、缘由，所以 occasion 还能表示理由。

normal.en: Occasional is the adjective for what happens only on some occasions.
normal.cn: occasional 是形容词，指只在某些场合才发生的事。

abstract.en: Time is not a flat line: some moments fall toward you and some slide past.
abstract.cn: 时间不是一条平线：有些时刻朝你落下，有些则滑了过去。

abstract.en: A special occasion is a day lifted out of the calendar and marked with care.
abstract.cn: 特殊场合是从日历里被拎出来、郑重标注的一天。

abstract.en: An occasion can be both the hour and the reason for gathering in it.
abstract.cn: occasion 既可以是那个时刻，也可以是让人聚到那一刻里来的理由。

examples.en: On that occasion she arrived an hour late.
examples.cn: 那一次她晚到了一个小时。

examples.en: The wedding was a grand occasion for the whole village.
examples.cn: 那场婚礼是全村的一件盛事。

examples.en: There is no occasion for alarm; the test is only a rehearsal.
examples.cn: 没有理由惊慌，这不过是一次演练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克神」——关键时刻像有神助；记住 occasion 是时机、场合。

root: 拉丁语 cadere（落下）→ occidere（落下、发生）→ occasio（落下的时刻、时机、缘由）→ 古法语 occasion → 英语 occasion；同族词 accident、cadence 也出自 cadere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a moment that falls; the senses run from a point in time to a marked event, then to the opening it offers, and finally to the reason behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落下的时刻」；义项从时间上的一点，走到被郑重标记的事件，再到它提供的开口，最后落到事情背后的缘由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watch hand stopping on one marked notch, the moment worth remembering.
core.cn: 核心意象：怀表指针停在某个刻度上，那一格正是值得记下的时刻。

branches.en: a late arrival still remembered years later
branches.cn: 多年后仍被提起的一次迟到

branches.en: villagers dressing up for a wedding
branches.cn: 村民为婚礼盛装

branches.en: a quiet hour opening for a word of thanks
branches.cn: 安静下来的一小时正好说几句感谢

branches.en: a doctor saying there is no cause to worry
branches.cn: 医生说没有理由担心

branches.en: a year-end dinner and the speech that gives it meaning
branches.cn: 年终晚宴，以及让这顿饭有意义的致辞

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb for falling, the compound it built, the Latin noun for a right moment, and two English suffixes that build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示落下的拉丁动词、由它构成的复合词、表示合适时刻的拉丁名词，以及两个分别造出形容词与副词的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere and its compound occidere lead to the noun occasio, and that noun is the direct parent of English occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 及其复合词 occidere 引出名词 occasio，而这个名词正是英语 occasion 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 小包；小袋；数据包；一大笔钱
definition_en: a small container made of paper or plastic holding a measured amount of something, a unit of data sent across a network, or, in British informal use, a large sum of money
core_image: 柜台上一个透明小袋被撕开一角，几块饼干从里面露出半边
scene: 便利店的柜台上摆着一个透明的小袋，里面装着几颗糖果。 He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
sceneCN: 这里的 packet 是「小包、小袋」（第 1 个义项：装少量物品的纸袋或塑料袋）；句意为他撕开一包饼干分给大家。图中可辨识物件：透明小袋、糖果、柜台。

pos.zh: 小包；小袋；数据包；一大笔钱

derivatives.zh: 由 packet（邮包）与 boat 复合而成，义为「定期邮船」
由 packet 与 switched 复合而成，义为「分组交换的」
由 packet 与 sniffer 复合而成，义为「数据包嗅探工具」

senses.title: A small paper or plastic container
senses.definition: a small container of paper, plastic or foil holding a measured amount of something such as biscuits, cigarettes or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、塑料或锡箔做成的小容器，装着一定量的饼干、香烟或种子等
senses.example: He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
senses.exampleCN: 他撕开一包饼干分给大家。
senses.why: Packet is a pack with a small ending on it: French -et marks something little, so the word means a little pack before it means anything else.
senses.whyCN: packet 是 pack 加上一个表示「小」的词尾：法语 -et 指小的东西，所以这个词最原始的意思就是「小包」。

senses.title: A unit of data sent across a network
senses.definition: a small unit into which a message is divided so that it can travel separately across a network
senses.definitionCN: 把信息切开后形成的小单元，使它能在网络中分别传输
senses.example: Each packet carries the address of its destination.
senses.exampleCN: 每个数据包都带着目的地的地址。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because a message is cut into small wrapped units, each addressed and sent alone, and the whole is rebuilt at the other end.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用这个词，是因为信息被切成一个个包好、写好地址、单独发送的小单元，到了另一端再重新拼起来。

senses.title: A large sum of money
senses.definition: a lot of money, used in British informal speech especially with the verbs cost and spend
senses.definitionCN: 很多钱，用于英式口语，常与 cost、spend 这类动词连用
senses.example: That new car must have cost a packet.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆新车一定花了一大笔钱。
senses.why: British slang stretched the little parcel in the opposite direction: what is small in size became heavy in price, so the modest packet turned into a serious amount of money.
senses.whyCN: 英式俚语把这个小包朝反方向拉：体积上小的东西变成价钱上重的，于是不起眼的一小包成了实打实的一大笔钱。

intro.en: Packet is a diminutive of pack, formed with the French ending -et; English has used it since the sixteenth century for a small parcel, for a mail boat, and in modern times for a unit of data.
intro.cn: packet 是 pack 的指小形式，由法语词尾 -et 构成；英语从十六世纪起用它指小包裹、邮政船，到了现代又用它指数据单元。

items.en: English pack meant a bundle tied up, a word usually traced to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pak.
items.cn: 英语 pack 指捆好的一包，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 pak。

items.en: The ending -et came through French, ultimately from a Latin diminutive, and it marks a smaller version of the base word.
items.cn: 词尾 -et 经法语传来，最终出自拉丁语的指小形式，用来标出比原词更小的东西。

items.en: Packet first meant a small parcel or a bundle of letters, and it was the ordinary word for a packet of papers.
items.cn: packet 最早指小包裹或一捆信件，当时是「一叠文件」的常用说法。

items.en: A packet boat was a ship that carried the mail packets, and the ship itself was soon shortened to packet.
items.cn: packet boat 指运送邮包的船，不久人们就干脆把这种船叫作 packet。

items.en: Modern English keeps the little container, adds the data packet of computing, and uses cost a packet for a very large price.
items.cn: 现代英语保留小容器义，加上计算机领域的数据包义，又用 cost a packet 表示价钱极高。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pack plus a small ending, with one false friend included; the near-meaning group collects words for small containers of goods.
note.cn: 形近组收由 pack 加指小词尾构成的词，并收入一个假朋友；近义组收表示装少量物品的小容器的词。

entries.definition: A bundle of things, or to put them into a container.
entries.definitionCN: 一捆东西，或把东西装进容器。

entries.definition: A wrapped parcel of any size, or a set of things sold together.
entries.definitionCN: 任意大小的包裹，或合在一起出售的一套东西。

entries.definition: A person or machine that packs goods.
entries.definitionCN: 打包的人或机器。

entries.definition: A small bag sewn into clothing for carrying things; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 缝在衣服里装东西的小袋；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small sealed bag holding a single portion of something.
entries.definitionCN: 装一份用量的密封小袋。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often closed with a drawstring.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的小袋，常用绳子收口。

entries.definition: A cardboard box or a sealed container for liquids.
entries.definitionCN: 纸板盒，或装液体的密封容器。

entries.definition: Something wrapped and tied, especially for post.
entries.definitionCN: 包好捆上的东西，尤指邮寄的包裹。

normalIntro.en: Packet is a pack shrunk by a French ending, so its hooks keep the picture of a small handful wrapped in paper or foil.
normalIntro.cn: packet 是被法语词尾缩小的 pack，记忆钩子保留「一小把东西裹在纸或锡箔里」的画面。

normal.en: Packet is pack plus the French diminutive -et, so the word says small pack in its very shape.
normal.cn: packet 是 pack 加法语指小词尾 -et，所以这个词的形状本身就在说「小包」。

normal.en: A packet is much smaller than a package: a packet fits in a pocket, while a package can need both arms.
normal.cn: packet 比 package 小得多：一包能塞进口袋，而一个包裹可能要双手才抱得住。

normal.en: Packet boat named a ship that carried the mail packets, and the ship later took the short name packet.
normal.cn: packet boat 指运送邮包的船，后来船本身也简称为 packet。

normal.en: British speakers say a packet of cigarettes where American speakers usually say a pack of cigarettes.
normal.cn: 英式英语说 a packet of cigarettes，而美式英语通常说 a pack of cigarettes。

normal.en: In computing the packet is wrapped, addressed and sent alone, which is why the postal picture transferred so easily.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，数据包被封装、写上地址、单独发送，所以邮政的画面能这么自然地搬过来。

abstract.en: A diminutive ending quietly tells us how much size matters in language: the same root can name a carton or a pocket-sized bag.
abstract.cn: 一个指小词尾悄悄说明尺寸在语言里多么重要：同一个词根既能指纸箱，也能指口袋大小的一包。

abstract.en: The same word holding a few biscuits and a unit of data suggests that a network is only a postal system made of light.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指几块饼干，也指一个数据单元，这说明网络不过是一个用光做的邮政系统。

abstract.en: Calling a huge bill a packet is a joke about size, and the joke works because the thing named is so small.
abstract.cn: 把巨额账单叫作一小包，是关于尺寸的玩笑，而这玩笑之所以成立，正因为被命名的东西如此之小。

examples.en: He tore open a packet of biscuits and shared them out.
examples.cn: 他撕开一包饼干分给大家。

examples.en: Each packet carries the address of its destination.
examples.cn: 每个数据包都带着目的地的地址。

examples.en: That new car must have cost a packet.
examples.cn: 那辆新车一定花了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克特」——派克特把一小把东西塞进纸袋，袋子只有巴掌大；记住 packet 是小包、小袋。

root: 由中古英语 pack（一捆，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或低地德语 pak）加法语指小词尾 -et 构成，十六世纪出现；与 package 同源，但 packet 指小容器，package 可指任意大小的包裹；词根属日耳曼语，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a little pack; the senses divide into the small container itself, the addressed units a network sends, and the slang use for a heavy price.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个小包；义项按「小容器本身」「网络发送的带地址单元」「俚语里的高额花费」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear little bag torn at one corner, biscuits showing through the opening.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一个透明小袋被撕开一角，几块饼干从里面露出半边。

branches.en: a bag of sweets standing by the till
branches.cn: 收银台边立着的一袋糖

branches.en: a torn corner and crumbs on a counter
branches.cn: 撕开的一角与柜台上的碎屑

branches.en: a message cut into pieces that travel apart
branches.cn: 被切成若干块分别传输的一条信息

branches.en: a label on each piece naming where it should go
branches.cn: 每一块上标明去向的标签

branches.en: the same small word for a bag and for a big bill
branches.cn: 同一个不起眼的小词，既指小袋，也指大账单

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for a bundle with a French ending for small things, so its parts say plainly a little bundle.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「捆」的日耳曼名词，加上法语中表示小东西的词尾，各部分明白地说出「一小捆」。

latinIntro.en: The root pack has no reliable Latin cognate; the small ending came through French and is only distantly Latin, so no Latin word is listed for this root.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 pack 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；指小词尾经法语传来，与拉丁语只有很远的关联，因此这一词根不列拉丁词。

a small bag sewn into clothing
items.meaningCN: 口袋；与 packet 只是拼写相近，词源不同

definition_zh: 一定的；开往…的；跳跃
definition_en: certain to happen or to do something
core_image: 被绳子系住、只能朝一个方向走
scene: 火车正开往北方。 The train is bound for the north.
sceneCN: 这里 bound 是「开往…的」（第 2 个义项：朝某个方向去）；句意是火车正开往北方。

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.definition: certain or very likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 确定或很可能发生
senses.example: Prices are bound to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 物价一定会涨。
senses.why: Being tied to an outcome means it cannot be avoided.
senses.whyCN: 被系在某个结果上，就无法避免。

senses.title: Travelling towards a place
senses.definition: going or heading towards a place
senses.definitionCN: 正朝着某地行进
senses.example: The train is bound for the north.
senses.exampleCN: 火车正开往北方。
senses.why: A traveller is tied to a destination, so the word names the direction.
senses.whyCN: 旅人被系在目的地之上，这个词便表示方向。

senses.title: To jump forward
senses.definition: to run with long energetic jumps
senses.definitionCN: 迈着大步有力地跳跃前进
senses.example: The deer bounded across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿跃过田野。
senses.why: This sense came from a French word meaning to leap.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自法语中表示跳跃的词。

intro.en: Two old words met in bound: one meant tied, the other meant to leap.
intro.cn: 两个古词在 bound 中汇合：一个表示系住，一个表示跳跃。

items.en: bunden was the past participle of bindan, to tie.
items.cn: bunden 是 bindan（捆）的过去分词。

items.en: bondir meant to leap or rebound.
items.cn: bondir 意为跳跃或弹回。

items.en: bound carried both the tied and the leaping senses.
items.cn: bound 同时带有「被系住」与「跳跃」两义。

items.en: bound for named the direction of a journey.
items.cn: bound for 指旅程的方向。

items.en: bound covers certainty, direction and jumping.
items.cn: 如今 bound 兼指必然、方向与跳跃。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names certainty and leaping.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是确定与跳跃。

entries.definition: a close connection
entries.definitionCN: 纽带

entries.definition: a small hill
entries.definitionCN: 小土丘

entries.definition: sure to happen
entries.definitionCN: 确定的

entries.definition: having no doubt
entries.definitionCN: 确信的

entries.definition: to jump a long way
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃

normalIntro.en: Bound is a rope: it ties you to a fate, a direction, or a jump.
normalIntro.cn: bound 是一根绳：把你系在命运、方向或一次跳跃上。

normal.en: Bound does not change for the adjective use.
normal.cn: 作形容词时 bound 没有词形变化。

normal.en: Be bound to means certain to happen.
normal.cn: be bound to 意为必定发生。

normal.en: A ship bound for Shanghai sails east.
normal.cn: 开往上海的船向东航行。

normal.en: A deer bounds across a field.
normal.cn: 鹿跃过田野。

normal.en: Boundary and boundless both grow from bound.
normal.cn: boundary 与 boundless 都由 bound 构成。

abstract.en: See a rope tied to a post.
abstract.cn: 想象一根系在柱子上的绳。

abstract.en: See a train sign naming one city.
abstract.cn: 想象火车上写着终点城市的牌子。

abstract.en: See a deer taking long jumps.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹿大步跃起。

examples.en: The train is bound for the north.
examples.cn: 火车正开往北方。

examples.en: Prices are bound to rise.
examples.cn: 物价一定会涨。

examples.en: The deer bounded across the field.
examples.cn: 鹿跃过田野。

dict_mnemonic.text: bound 与 bind 同源：被绑住就逃不掉，所以是「一定」；被绑向某地，就是「开往」。

root: bound 由两个来源汇合：古英语 bindan（捆）的过去分词表示被系住、必然，古法语 bondir 表示跳跃，两义在中古英语合并。

sensesIntro.en: Certainty, a direction of travel, and a long springing jump.
sensesIntro.cn: 必然、行进的方向，以及有力的跳跃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tied to a post.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在柱子上的绳子。

branches.en: bound to happen
branches.cn: 必然发生

branches.en: bound up with
branches.cn: 与…密切相关

branches.en: bound for home
branches.cn: 开往家乡

branches.en: northbound
branches.cn: 向北的

branches.en: bound across the field
branches.cn: 跃过田野

intro.en: Bound makes boundary, boundless and unbounded.
intro.cn: bound 可构成 boundary、boundless 与 unbounded。
