latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的词只在意思上相关。

items.meaning: a line that marks a limit
certain to have a particular future

definition_zh: 节奏；韵律；规律
definition_en: a regular pattern of sounds or movements
core_image: 鼓面上一圈圈震动的波纹
scene: 鼓手让鼓点保持稳定的节奏，舞者跟着脚步移动。 The drummer kept a steady rhythm, and the dancers moved with the beat.
sceneCN: 这里 rhythm 是「节奏」（第 1 个义项：声音有规律的重复）；句意：鼓手让鼓点保持稳定的节奏，舞者跟着脚步移动。

senses.title: Sound pattern
senses.definition: a regular repeated pattern of sound
senses.definitionCN: 声音有规律的重复模式
senses.example: The song has a fast rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌节奏很快。
senses.why: The Greek word rhythmos means measured flow.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 rhythmos 意为有节制的流动。

senses.title: Regular movement
senses.definition: a regular pattern of movement
senses.definitionCN: 动作的有规律重复
senses.example: The rowers found a common rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 划桨手找到了共同的节奏。
senses.why: Any repeated motion can be called a rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 任何重复的动作都可称为节奏。

senses.title: Daily pattern
senses.definition: a regular way in which things happen
senses.definitionCN: 事物有规律的发生方式
senses.example: Her days follow a calm rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的日子遵循平静的规律。
senses.why: The idea spreads from music to the pattern of life.
senses.whyCN: 这一概念从音乐延伸到生活规律。

intro.en: Rhythm comes from Greek rhythmos, measured motion, from rhein, to flow.
intro.cn: rhythm 源自希腊语 rhythmos（有节制的运动），来自 rhein（流动）。

items.en: Rhythmos means measured flow.
items.cn: rhythmos 意为有节制的流动。

items.en: Rhein means to flow.
items.cn: rhein 意为流动。

items.en: Rhythmus keeps the Greek form.
items.cn: rhythmus 保留了希腊语形式。

items.en: French rithme shapes the spelling.
items.cn: 法语 rithme 塑造了拼写。

items.en: Rhythm loses some Greek letters but keeps the beat.
items.cn: rhythm 丢掉了部分希腊字母，却保留了节拍。

note.en: Rhythm is the pattern; a beat is one pulse inside it.
note.cn: rhythm 是整体模式；beat 是其中一个脉冲。

entries.definition: having a regular beat
entries.definitionCN: 有节奏的

entries.definition: matching sounds at line ends
entries.definitionCN: 押韵

entries.definition: an irregular heartbeat
entries.definitionCN: 心律不齐

entries.definition: one hit in a regular series
entries.definitionCN: 节拍

entries.definition: the speed of a piece of music
entries.definitionCN: 速度

entries.definition: a repeated design or order
entries.definitionCN: 模式

normalIntro.en: Rhythm is the heartbeat of music and of days.
normalIntro.cn: rhythm 是音乐与日子的心跳。

normal.en: A steady rhythm keeps dancers together.
normal.cn: 稳定的节奏让舞者整齐一致。

normal.en: The song has a lively rhythm.
normal.cn: 这首歌节奏活泼。

normal.en: Body rhythm changes when we are tired.
normal.cn: 疲倦时身体节律会改变。

normal.en: Keep the rhythm means do not speed up.
normal.cn: keep the rhythm 意为不要加速。

normal.en: Compare beat: a beat is one hit, a rhythm is the whole pattern.
normal.cn: 对比 beat：beat 是一下敲击，rhythm 是整个模式。

abstract.en: Picture ripples spreading from a drum.
abstract.cn: 想象鼓面上一圈圈扩散的波纹。

abstract.en: Imagine waves meeting the shore at equal intervals.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪以相等间隔拍岸。

abstract.en: Think of a clock ticking inside a song.
abstract.cn: 想象歌声里有一只钟在滴答走动。

examples.en: The drummer lost the rhythm for a moment.
examples.cn: 鼓手有一瞬间失去了节奏。

examples.en: Her writing has a natural rhythm.
examples.cn: 她的文字有自然的韵律。

examples.en: The city has its own daily rhythm.
examples.cn: 这座城市有自己的日常节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rhythm」中间只有一个元音——把单词当作鼓点来记：六个字母，两拍落下。

root: 希腊语 rhythmos（有节制的流动）← rhein（流动）→ 拉丁语 rhythmus → 法语 rithme → rhythm。

sensesIntro.en: Rhythm begins as a pattern of sound, extends to repeated movement, and finally to the regular pattern of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: rhythm 从声音模式开始，延伸到重复的动作，最后指日常生活的规律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples spreading from a drumhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓面上一圈圈扩散的波纹。

branches.en: Sound is the first home of rhythm.
branches.cn: 声音是节奏最初的家。

branches.en: Repeated movement carries the same pattern.
branches.cn: 重复的动作承载同样的模式。

branches.en: Daily life also has a regular beat.
branches.cn: 日常生活也有规律的节拍。

branches.en: Music and motion share one pattern.
branches.cn: 音乐与动作共用一个模式。

branches.en: Bodies and days both repeat in time.
branches.cn: 身体与日子都在时间中重复。

intro.en: Rhythm carries the Greek root rhy, meaning to flow.
intro.cn: rhythm 带有希腊词根 rhy，意为流动。

latinIntro.en: Greek rhythmos passed into Latin as rhythmus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 rhythmos 以 rhythmus 的形式进入拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Rhythmus carries the Greek word into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rhythmus 把希腊词带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 结果；影响；效果；作用；使产生
definition_en: a result produced by a cause, an impression made on the senses, the state of being in force, or to bring something about
core_image: 一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈向外推开
scene: 演出进行到一半，舞台灯光忽然压暗，观众席一片安静。 The lighting effect made the whole hall hold its breath.
sceneCN: 这里 effect 是「感官印象、效果」（第 2 个义项：灯光、声音等在人眼中或耳中造成的印象）；句意是灯光效果让整个大厅屏住了呼吸。

pos.zh: 名词：结果；影响；效果；作用；效力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「有效的；生效的」
由 effective 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有效地；实际上」
由 effective 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「有效性」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ual 构成，义为「奏效的；有效力的」

senses.title: A result of a cause
senses.definition: a change or result that is produced by an action, event or cause
senses.definitionCN: 由某个行为、事件或原因所造成的变化或结果
senses.example: The medicine had no effect on the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药对退烧没有效果。
senses.why: Effect is Latin effectus, a thing done; a cause does something, and what it leaves behind is the effect.
senses.whyCN: effect 源自拉丁语 effectus，意为「做成之事」；原因做出某事，留在后面的东西就是结果。

senses.title: An impression on the senses
senses.definition: an impression produced on the eye, ear or mind, especially by light, sound or colour
senses.definitionCN: 尤指光线、声音或色彩在视觉、听觉或心理上造成的印象
senses.example: The film uses simple sound effects to build tension.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片用简单的音效营造紧张感。
senses.why: A stage light or a drumbeat does something to the audience, so the result it leaves in the senses is also an effect.
senses.whyCN: 舞台灯光或鼓点对观众做了某件事，于是在感官里留下的结果同样是一种 effect。

senses.title: The state of being in force
senses.definition: the state of being active or legally valid, as of a rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 规则或协议等处于运作或法律上有效的状态
senses.example: The new tax is now in effect.
senses.exampleCN: 新税现已生效。
senses.why: A law that has been made is a thing done; once it is in effect, that done thing stands and works.
senses.whyCN: 制定好的法律是一件「做成之事」；一旦 in effect，这件做成之事就立在那里并发挥作用。

senses.title: To bring something about
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to bring it into being
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或使其成为现实
senses.example: The manager effected a complete change of policy.
senses.exampleCN: 经理促成了政策的彻底改变。
senses.why: As a verb, effect names the act of doing the thing itself, not the result that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，effect 指「把这件事做出来」的动作本身，而不是随后留下的结果。

intro.en: Effect comes from Latin efficere, to do or bring about, through effectus, a thing done, and reached English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: effect 来自拉丁语 efficere（做出、完成），经分词 effectus（做成之事）与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the core of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的核心。

items.en: Ex- meaning out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出来、完成」。

items.en: The participle effectus meant accomplished or brought about, and became a noun for the result.
items.cn: 分词 effectus 意为「已完成的、已做成的」，后来成为表示结果的名词。

items.en: Old French effect kept both the noun of result and the sense of accomplishment.
items.cn: 古法语 effect 同时保留了「结果」的名词义与「完成」的意味。

items.en: English first used it for a result and later for an impression and a rule in force.
items.cn: 英语先用它表示结果，后来扩展出感官印象与法规生效两义。

items.en: The verb use, to effect a change, settled beside the noun in formal style.
items.cn: 动词用法「促成一项改变」在正式文体中与名词用法并存固定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on effect and its easily confused partner affect; the near-meaning group separates result, consequence and impact.
note.cn: 形近组收由 effect 构成的词以及易混的 affect；近义组区分 result、consequence 与 impact。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to produce the wanted result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，由 effect 加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a way that succeeds, or in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有效地、实际上」，由 effective 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to influence or to move emotionally; often confused with effect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响、使感动」，常与 effect 混淆。

entries.definition: Something that follows from an action; plainer and more general than effect.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，比 effect 更普通、更泛。

entries.definition: A result, often an indirect or unwelcome one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果」，常指间接或不受欢迎的结果。

entries.definition: A strong effect or influence on something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲击、重大影响」，强调力度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from one cause and follow its ripple outward into sensed impressions, standing laws and deliberate action.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个原因出发，顺着涟漪走到感官印象、生效的法规与有意的行动。

normal.en: Effect is what a cause leaves behind.
normal.cn: effect 就是原因留在身后的东西。

normal.en: Sound effects are effects you hear, not results you measure.
normal.cn: sound effects 是你听见的效果，不是你去测量的结果。

normal.en: A rule in effect is a done thing still standing.
normal.cn: in effect 的规则就是一件做成之事仍立在那里。

normal.en: To effect a change is to do it; to affect something is to touch it.
normal.cn: to effect a change 是把它做出来；to affect 是触碰、影响它。

normal.en: Cause and effect are the two ends of one sentence.
normal.cn: 原因与结果是同一个句子的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水。

abstract.en: The same ripple can be seen, heard, or written into a law.
abstract.cn: 同一圈涟漪可以被看见、被听见，也可以被写进一条法律。

abstract.en: Effect is the mark left by something that acted.
abstract.cn: effect 就是某个东西行动之后留下的印记。

examples.en: The medicine had no effect on the fever.
examples.cn: 这种药对退烧没有效果。

examples.en: The film uses simple sound effects to build tension.
examples.cn: 这部影片用简单的音效营造紧张感。

examples.en: The manager effected a complete change of policy.
examples.cn: 经理促成了政策的彻底改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊费克特」——石子落水，涟漪一圈圈推开

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加前缀 ex-「出」构成 efficere「做出、完成」，其分词 effectus 转为「做成之事」，经古法语 effect 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of effect: a result left by a cause, an impression on the senses, a rule that is in force, and the verb of bringing something about.
sensesIntro.cn: effect 的四个义项：原因留下的结果、感官上的印象、生效的规则，以及「使某事发生」的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into still water, with rings spreading outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈向外推开。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what the cause leaves behind.
branches.cn: 结果线：原因留在身后的东西。

branches.en: THE IMPRESSION: the ripple felt by eye or ear.
branches.cn: 印象线：被眼睛或耳朵接住的那圈涟漪。

branches.en: THE FORCE: a made rule still standing.
branches.cn: 效力线：已制定的规则仍立在那里。

branches.en: THE ACT: doing the thing itself.
branches.cn: 动作线：把这件事本身做出来。

branches.en: ONE PROCESS: the measurable result and the sensed impression both come from the same cause.
branches.cn: 同一过程：可测量的结果与被感知的印象都来自同一个原因。

intro.en: Effect is a Latin verb turned noun; English builds a small family of adjectives and adverbs on the same stem.
intro.cn: effect 是由拉丁语动词转成的名词；英语在同一词干上构成一小族形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, efficere and effectus are all recorded, so only deeper roots are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、efficere 与 effectus 均有记录，只有更早的词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It is the base of efficere.
It is the direct source verb.

definition_zh: 空白的；茫然的；空白处
definition_en: empty, with nothing written or printed on it
core_image: 一张没有写字的纸
scene: 桌上摊着一张什么都没写的纸。 She stared at the blank page for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 blank 是「空白的」（第 1 个义项：没有写字或印刷内容）；句意是她对着空白的一页看了一个小时。

senses.title: With nothing written
senses.definition: having no writing, print or marks
senses.definitionCN: 没有文字、印刷内容或标记的
senses.example: She stared at the blank page for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她对着空白的一页看了一个小时。
senses.why: White paper looked empty, so the colour word became the word for empty.
senses.whyCN: 白纸看起来空无一物，于是这个颜色词成了「空白」的意思。

senses.title: Showing no expression
senses.definition: showing no understanding, feeling or reaction
senses.definitionCN: 没有理解、情绪或反应的
senses.example: He gave me a blank look.
senses.exampleCN: 他茫然地看了我一眼。
senses.why: An empty face was described like empty paper.
senses.whyCN: 空无一物的表情，被比作空白的纸。

senses.title: An empty space to fill
senses.definition: an empty space left for an answer or signature
senses.definitionCN: 留待填写答案或签名的空白处
senses.example: Fill in the blank with one word.
senses.exampleCN: 用一个词填空。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the empty space itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，直接指那块空着的地方。

intro.en: Blank came from a French word for white and gradually meant empty.
intro.cn: blank 来自法语中表示白色的词，后来逐渐转为「空的」。

items.en: blank meant white and shining.
items.cn: blank 意为白色而发亮的。

items.en: blanc carried the sense of white.
items.cn: blanc 保留了白色的意思。

items.en: blank entered English as white or pale.
items.cn: blank 以「白色、苍白」之义进入英语。

items.en: blank came to mean an empty space on paper.
items.cn: blank 开始指纸上的空白处。

items.en: blank covers empty paper and an empty expression.
items.cn: 如今 blank 兼指空白纸张与茫然神情。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives other words for emptiness.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是表示「空」的词。

entries.definition: the darkest colour
entries.definitionCN: 黑色

entries.definition: plain and without strong taste
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无味的

entries.definition: to close the eyes for a moment
entries.definitionCN: 眨眼

entries.definition: holding or containing nothing
entries.definitionCN: 空的

entries.definition: not occupied by anyone
entries.definitionCN: 空着的

entries.definition: a completely empty space
entries.definitionCN: 虚空

normalIntro.en: Blank is a white page waiting for something to be written.
normalIntro.cn: blank 是一张等着被写字的白色纸页。

normal.en: A blank page has no writing at all.
normal.cn: a blank page 上什么字都没有。

normal.en: Go blank describes a mind that stops.
normal.cn: go blank 形容脑子突然一片空白。

normal.en: Blanks in a test are spaces to fill.
normal.cn: 试卷里的 blanks 是待填的空格。

normal.en: The adverb is blankly.
normal.cn: 副词是 blankly。

normal.en: Black is dark; blank is empty.
normal.cn: black 是黑，blank 是空。

abstract.en: See a sheet of paper with nothing on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张什么都没有的白纸。

abstract.en: See a face that shows no reaction.
abstract.cn: 想象一张毫无反应的脸。

abstract.en: See a line of dashes waiting for answers.
abstract.cn: 想象一排等待填写的横线。

examples.en: She stared at the blank page for an hour.
examples.cn: 她对着空白的一页看了一个小时。

examples.en: He gave me a blank look.
examples.cn: 他茫然地看了我一眼。

examples.en: Fill in the blank with one word.
examples.cn: 用一个词填空。

dict_mnemonic.text: black 是黑，blank 是空，黑板擦干净以后，剩下的就是 blank。

root: blank 源自古法语 blanc（白色的），更早出自法兰克语；中古英语先表示白色、苍白，十六世纪起转指纸上的空白处，又引申出茫然、无表情的意思。

sensesIntro.en: White paper became empty paper, and an empty paper became an empty face.
sensesIntro.cn: 白纸变成空白的纸，空白的纸又变成空白的神情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper with nothing written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张什么都没写的纸。

branches.en: a blank page
branches.cn: 空白页

branches.en: a blank screen
branches.cn: 空白的屏幕

branches.en: a blank look
branches.cn: 茫然的表情

branches.en: fill in the blanks
branches.cn: 填空

branches.en: leave a blank
branches.cn: 留出空白

intro.en: Blank takes -ly and -ness without changing its stem.
intro.cn: blank 加 -ly 与 -ness 时词干不变。

latinIntro.en: The base comes from a Germanic word that French passed on.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自一个日耳曼语词，由法语转手传入英语。

definition_zh: 演示；证明；示威
definition_en: to show how something works, to prove a fact, or to gather in public protest
core_image: 讲台上的人举起一个装置，向所有人展示它怎样运转
scene: 实验室里，学生把一壶水烧开，让蒸汽推动小轮子转起来。 The teacher demonstrated how the pump works.
sceneCN: 这里 demonstrate 指「演示」（第 1 个义项：把做法或运转方式展示给人看）；句意是老师演示了这台泵如何工作。

senses.title: Show how something works
senses.definition: to show someone how to do something or how a thing works
senses.definitionCN: 向某人展示做法或某物如何运转
senses.example: The teacher demonstrated how the pump works.
senses.exampleCN: 老师演示了这台泵如何工作。
senses.why: A thing understood by the eye is faster than a page of words.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛看懂的东西，比一页文字来得快。

senses.title: Prove with evidence
senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 清楚地表明某事为真
senses.example: The study demonstrates a link between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究证明了睡眠与记忆之间的联系。
senses.why: A proof is a showing that leaves no room for doubt.
senses.whyCN: 证明就是让人没有余地怀疑的展示。

senses.title: March in public protest
senses.definition: to gather in public to show strong disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 在公共场合聚集以表达强烈反对
senses.example: Thousands demonstrated against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人示威反对这项新税。
senses.why: A crowd also demonstrates when it shows its opinion in the street.
senses.whyCN: 人群走上街头把意见展示出来，也是一种示威。

intro.en: Demonstrate comes from Latin monstrare, to show, with de- adding force; it entered English through the schools.
intro.cn: demonstrate 来自拉丁语 monstrare（展示），前缀 de- 加强语气，经学术用语进入英语。

items.en: Monstrare meant to point out or show, and de- added force to it.
items.cn: monstrare 意为指出或展示，de- 给它加上力度。

items.en: Scholars used demonstrare for proving a point by clear signs.
items.cn: 学者用 demonstrare 表示以清楚的迹象证明一点。

items.en: English took demonstrate for showing a fact by argument or experiment.
items.cn: 英语借来 demonstrate，指用论证或实验展示一个事实。

items.en: The sense of marching in public grew with mass politics.
items.cn: 随着大众政治兴起，走上街头这一层意思长了出来。

items.en: It now covers proof, teaching and street protest alike.
items.cn: 如今它同时覆盖证明、教学与街头抗议。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the demonstr- stem, and the meaning group moves from showing to proving to protesting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 demonstr- 这个词干，近义组则从展示走到证明，再走到抗议。

entries.definition: the act of showing or protesting
entries.definitionCN: 展示或示威的行为

entries.definition: showing feelings openly
entries.definitionCN: 公开表露感情的

entries.definition: a person who shows or protests
entries.definitionCN: 演示者或示威者

entries.definition: to let someone see something
entries.definitionCN: 让某人看见某物

entries.definition: to establish that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 确立某事为真

entries.definition: to say or show that you disagree
entries.definitionCN: 说出或表明自己不同意

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand turning a small wheel and end with a crowd holding signs in the street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手转动小轮子开始，落到街上举着牌子的人群。

normal.en: A pump shown once teaches more than a page of description.
normal.cn: 把泵演示一遍，胜过一页说明。

normal.en: To demonstrate is to put the proof where the eye can reach it.
normal.cn: demonstrate 就是把证据放到眼睛够得着的地方。

normal.en: A crowd with signs is also showing something, only louder.
normal.cn: 举牌的人群也在展示，只是声音更大。

normal.en: Monstrare is the old word for pointing at a thing.
normal.cn: monstrare 就是古时候「指着某物」的说法。

normal.en: The teacher demonstrates, the student repeats, the fact stays.
normal.cn: 老师演示，学生重复，事实就留下了。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pointing at a wheel that begins to turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指指着一个开始转动的轮子。

abstract.en: Picture a chart laid flat so everyone can see the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图表被摊平，让所有人都看见同一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a row of signs lifted above a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一排牌子被举到人群之上。

examples.en: The teacher demonstrated how the pump works.
examples.cn: 老师演示了这台泵如何工作。

examples.en: The study demonstrates a link between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 这项研究证明了睡眠与记忆之间的联系。

examples.en: Thousands demonstrated against the new tax.
examples.cn: 数千人示威反对这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 demonstrate 记成「demo 加 strate」：demo 是展示，把事情摆到台面上给人看，就是演示与证明。

root: 来自拉丁语 demonstrare，由 de-（加强）与 monstrare（指出、展示）组成。它先用于以清楚迹象证明一个论点，十六世纪进入英语后泛指展示；十九世纪大众政治兴起，又添上走上街头表达反对的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a hand showing a working model, to a study proving a fact, to a crowd showing its anger.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只手展示运转的模型，到一项研究证明事实，再到人群展示愤怒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifts a small machine so every eye can follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手举起小机器，让每双眼睛都能跟上。

branches.en: The first sense is a model shown until the working is clear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把模型展示到运转方式变清楚。

branches.en: The second sense is a fact placed where no one can miss it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把事实摆到没人能忽略的位置。

branches.en: The third sense is an opinion carried into the street.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把意见带到街上。

branches.en: Showing and proving both depend on making something visible.
branches.cn: 展示与证明都靠把某样东西变得可见。

branches.en: A sign in a march is also evidence of what people feel.
branches.cn: 游行中的一块牌子，也是人们感受的证据。

intro.en: Demonstrate has a Latin spine and grows nouns for the act, the person and the quality of being provable.
intro.cn: demonstrate 有一根拉丁脊梁，长出了表示行为、人物与可证明性的名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is monstrare, to show; de- strengthens it and -tion turns the act into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是 monstrare（展示），de- 加强语气，-tion 把行为变成名词。

items.meaning: a showing, a proof or a protest
items.example: The demonstration drew a large crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这场示威吸引了一大群人。
一位演示者讲解了这台机器。
他是一位感情外露的父亲。
这种收益是可以证明的。

items.meaning: in a way that can be shown
not yet shown to be true
items.exampleCN: 这一主张仍未得到证明。

definition_zh: 向后地；倒着；退步
definition_en: toward the back, or in the opposite order
core_image: 一段录像被倒着播放，水往杯子里回去
scene: 视频播放器被人按了回放键。 The film ran backwards for a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 backwards 是「倒着」（第 2 个义项：顺序相反地）；句意是影片倒着放了几秒钟。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「向后的」，backwards 为其副词形式
由 backward 加 -ness 构成，义为「落后」

senses.title: Toward the back
senses.definition: in the direction of the back
senses.definitionCN: 朝背部的方向
senses.example: She stepped backwards without looking.
senses.exampleCN: 她没看就向后退了一步。
senses.why: Backwards is the adverb form of backward, and the -s ending marks an old genitive that became part of the word.
senses.whyCN: backwards 是 backward 的副词形式，词尾的 -s 原是古属格标记，后来固定进了单词。

senses.title: In reverse order
senses.definition: in the opposite order or direction
senses.definitionCN: 以相反的顺序或方向
senses.example: The film ran backwards for a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 影片倒着放了几秒钟。
senses.why: Moving backwards reverses space, and the same reversal applies to time and order, so counting and reading can also go backwards.
senses.whyCN: 向后移动反转了空间，同样的反转也适用于时间与顺序，所以数数和阅读也能倒着来。

senses.title: Making no progress
senses.definition: toward a worse or earlier state
senses.definitionCN: 朝更糟或更早的状态
senses.example: The business went backwards last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年倒退了。
senses.why: If forward is progress, moving backwards is losing ground, which gives the figurative sense of decline.
senses.whyCN: 如果说 forward 是进步，那么往后退就是失地，于是有了「退步」的比喻义。

intro.en: Backwards is an old direction word with a settled -s ending.
intro.cn: backwards 是一个词尾带 -s 的古老方向词。

items.en: bæc meant 'the back'.
items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: bakward meant 'toward the back'.
items.cn: bakward 意为「朝向后方」。

items.en: the -s form became a separate adverb.
items.cn: 带 -s 的形式成为独立副词。

items.en: backwards and backward both served as adverbs.
items.cn: backwards 与 backward 都曾作副词。

items.en: British English prefers backwards, American English backward.
items.cn: 英式英语多用 backwards，美式多用 backward。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -wards ending; the near-meaning group gives reverse and rearward words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -wards 结尾；近义组是表示反向与后方的词。

entries.definition: toward the back
entries.definitionCN: 向后的

entries.definition: in the direction of
entries.definitionCN: 朝向

entries.definition: after an event
entries.definitionCN: 后来

entries.definition: in the opposite order
entries.definitionCN: 相反地

entries.definition: toward the rear
entries.definitionCN: 向后

entries.definition: in an opposite way
entries.definitionCN: 反向地

normalIntro.en: Backwards can reverse a step, a count or a whole business.
normalIntro.cn: backwards 能让一步、一段数数或整桩生意反过来。

normal.en: British English uses backwards for the adverb more often than backward.
normal.cn: 英式英语副词更常用 backwards。

normal.en: Count backwards from ten is a common classroom task.
normal.cn: 从十倒着数是常见的课堂任务。

normal.en: Backwards and forwards means moving to and fro.
normal.cn: backwards and forwards 意为来回移动。

normal.en: The word always ends in -s.
normal.cn: 这个词总以 -s 结尾。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BACK-wards.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a film playing in reverse.
abstract.cn: 想象一段倒着播放的影片。

abstract.en: See a number line read from right to left.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从右往左读的数轴。

abstract.en: See a walker leaving heel prints first.
abstract.cn: 想象走路的人先留下脚跟印。

examples.en: She stepped backwards without looking.
examples.cn: 她没看就向后退了一步。

examples.en: The film ran backwards for a few seconds.
examples.cn: 影片倒着放了几秒钟。

examples.en: The business went backwards last year.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年倒退了。

dict_mnemonic.text: back（后面）加 -ward（朝向）加 -s：朝着背后去，也可以把顺序整个倒过来。

root: 由中古英语 bakward 加副词性词尾 -s 构成；back 源自古英语 bæc「背部」，-ward 意为「朝向」；由「向后」引申为「倒着」与「退步」。

sensesIntro.en: Going back, reversing order and losing ground are one movement read in space, time and value.
sensesIntro.cn: 向后退、把顺序倒过来与失去进展，是同一种移动在空间、时间与价值上的读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a film playing in reverse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段倒着播放的影片。

branches.en: walk backwards
branches.cn: 倒退着走

branches.en: lean backwards
branches.cn: 向后仰

branches.en: count backwards
branches.cn: 倒着数

branches.cn: 退步

intro.cn: 后缀 -wards 在副词中标记方向，如 backwards 与 upwards。

definition_zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线
definition_en: a narrow road or path; one of the marked strips of a road, track or pool; a fixed route used by ships or aircraft
core_image: 村口一条窄路，两旁是石墙和伸出来的树枝
scene: 雨后的村子很安静，一条窄巷两边的石墙被淋得发亮。 She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
sceneCN: 这里是「小路、小巷」（第 1 个义项：狭窄的道路）；句意是她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。图中可辨识物件：石墙、湿路面、树枝。

pos.zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线

derivatives.zh: 由 lane 与 way 复合而成，义为「小巷；巷道」
由 multi- 与 lane 复合而成，义为「多车道的」
由 two 与 lane 复合而成，义为「双车道的」

senses.title: A narrow road or path
senses.definition: a narrow road, especially one in the countryside or between buildings
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄的道路，尤指乡间或建筑物之间的小路
senses.example: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。
senses.why: Old English lane named a narrow path, and narrowness remains the clearest feature of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，而「窄」至今仍是这个义项最鲜明的特征。

senses.title: A marked strip of a road
senses.definition: one of the marked strips into which a road is divided for traffic
senses.definitionCN: 道路为车辆行驶而划分出的标线通道之一
senses.example: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。
senses.why: Once roads were painted and divided, the old word for a narrow path was ready-made for a narrow strip of traffic.
senses.whyCN: 道路画上线并划分之后，原指窄路的旧词正好用来指窄窄的一条车行道。

senses.title: A marked strip of a track or pool
senses.definition: one of the parallel strips used for racing on a track or in a swimming pool
senses.definitionCN: 田径场或游泳池中供比赛使用的平行分道
senses.example: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。
senses.why: A pool is divided into parallel strips so that swimmers do not collide, and each strip is a narrow path of water.
senses.whyCN: 泳池被分成平行的条带，避免游泳者相互碰撞，而每一条带都是水上的一条窄路。

senses.title: A fixed route for ships or aircraft
senses.definition: a fixed route that ships or aircraft regularly follow
senses.definitionCN: 船只或飞机固定沿用的路线
senses.example: Ships follow a busy lane across the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 船只沿着一条繁忙的航道穿过海峡。
senses.why: A route is also a long narrow strip on a map, so lane extends naturally from a path on land to a path at sea or in the air.
senses.whyCN: 航线在地图上同样是一条狭长的带，所以 lane 从陆上小路自然延伸到海上或空中的路线。

intro.en: Lane is a Germanic word for a narrow path; English has kept the narrowness and applied it to traffic, races and sea routes.
intro.cn: lane 是日耳曼语中指窄路的词；英语保留了「窄」的特征，并把它用到车道、赛道和航线。

items.en: The word is Germanic in origin; a related form is reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，可重构出相关形式，但确切形态并不确定。

items.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path or road, often one between hedges or fields.
items.cn: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，常是树篱或田地之间的一条路。

items.en: Middle English kept lane for country paths and for the narrow streets of a town.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lane 指乡间小路和城里的窄街。

items.en: With modern roads and racing, lane was applied to marked strips of traffic, tracks and pools.
items.cn: 随着现代道路与赛事的出现，lane 被用来指标出的车道、跑道和泳道。

items.en: Modern English also uses lane for fixed shipping and air routes.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 lane 指固定的航线和航道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and one sound-alike; the near-meaning group collects other narrow ways through space.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词和一个同音词；近义组收其他穿越空间的狭窄道路。

entries.definition: The past participle of lie, as in having lain down; it sounds the same but belongs to a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 lie 的过去分词，如「已经躺下」；它与 lane 同音，但属于另一个动词。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or service road, common in Australian and New Zealand English.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的通道或服务性小路，常见于澳大利亚与新西兰英语。

entries.definition: Tall and thin in an awkward way; only the spelling is close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦高而显得笨拙的；只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Having several marked strips for traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有数条标线车道的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between or behind buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间或后方的一条窄通道。

entries.definition: A track worn by feet or made for walking.
entries.definitionCN: 被人踩出或专为行走而修的小径。

entries.definition: A wide way for vehicles, usually much broader than a lane.
entries.definitionCN: 供车辆行驶的宽阔道路，通常比 lane 宽得多。

entries.definition: A rough path or a prepared course for racing.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小路，或为比赛修整好的跑道。

normalIntro.en: The word stays tied to narrowness; compounds count strips, and the same shape is read on roads, pools and maps.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词始终与「窄」相连；复合词数出条带的数量，而同样的形状在道路、泳池和地图上都能看到。

normal.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path, which is why a country lane is still narrower than a road.
normal.cn: 古英语 lane 指窄路，所以乡间 lane 至今仍比 road 窄。

normal.en: Lain is a homophone but not a relative: it is the past participle of lie, meaning to rest flat.
normal.cn: lain 是同音词而不是同族词：它是 lie 的过去分词，意为平躺。

normal.en: Laneway adds way to lane, and it is the usual word for a narrow service passage in Australasian English.
normal.cn: laneway 在 lane 后加 way，是澳新英语中表示狭窄通道的常用词。

normal.en: Multi-lane and two-lane count the marked strips, so the compound tells you how many streams of traffic there are.
normal.cn: multi-lane 和 two-lane 数的是标线通道，所以复合词直接说明有几股车流。

normal.en: A bus lane is a marked strip reserved for buses, which shows how far lane has moved from a country path.
normal.cn: bus lane 是留给公交车的标线通道，由此可见 lane 已从乡间小路走出多远。

abstract.en: A lane is a line cut through space, whether grass, asphalt or water, and that is why one word serves all of them.
abstract.cn: lane 是在空间里划出的一条线，无论在草地、柏油还是水面上，所以一个词能服务所有这些场景。

abstract.en: Narrowness separates a lane from a road, just as a single track separates one life from another.
abstract.cn: 窄，把 lane 与 road 区分开，就像单条轨迹把一种人生与另一种分开。

abstract.en: Down memory lane shows that a path can also run through time rather than through land.
abstract.cn: down memory lane 说明道路也可以穿过时间，而不只是穿过土地。

examples.en: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
examples.cn: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。

examples.en: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
examples.cn: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。

examples.en: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
examples.cn: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「雷恩」——人名雷恩总爱走乡间小路；lane 是小路。

root: 古英语 lane，属日耳曼语固有词，指狭窄的道路；与拉丁语无可靠同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Narrow passage is the core; it widens into traffic strips, racing strips and routes drawn across sea or sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是狭窄的通道；它扩展成车道、赛道，以及画在海面或天空上的航线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path between two stone walls, just wide enough for one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：两道石墙之间的一条窄路，只容一人走过。

branches.en: a country path with hedges on both sides
branches.cn: 两旁是树篱的乡间小路

branches.en: a town passage too narrow for two carts
branches.cn: 窄得容不下两辆马车的城中通道

branches.en: painted lines splitting a wide road
branches.cn: 把宽路分开的油漆标线

branches.en: ropes floating across a swimming pool
branches.cn: 横在泳池里的浮标绳

branches.en: a dotted route drawn across a chart of the sea
branches.cn: 在海图上画出的一条虚线航线

intro.en: A Germanic noun forms one compound with way, one prefix compound with multi-, and one counting compound with two.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词分别与 way、前缀 multi- 和数词 two 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

a narrow road in the countryside

definition_zh: 破坏；毁灭；摧毁
definition_en: the act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed
core_image: 大风过后，屋顶只剩几根横梁对着天
scene: 洪水退去后，街上堆着断掉的木梁和碎瓦。 The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
sceneCN: 这里 destruction 指「破坏」（第 1 个义项：被彻底毁坏的状态与痕迹）；句意是这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。

senses.title: The state of being wrecked
senses.definition: the state of having been badly damaged or completely ruined
senses.definitionCN: 已被严重损坏或彻底毁掉的状态
senses.example: The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。
senses.why: After the force passes, the damage stays behind as a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 那股力量过去之后，损坏留在原地，成了一道风景。

senses.title: The act of tearing down
senses.definition: the deliberate act of destroying a building or an object
senses.definitionCN: 有意把建筑或物体毁掉的行为
senses.example: The destruction of the old bridge took two days.
senses.exampleCN: 拆除那座旧桥花了两天。
senses.why: Someone has to decide, bring tools and begin.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人下决定、带工具，然后动手。

senses.title: The thing that ruins you
senses.definition: a person or quality that causes someone's downfall
senses.definitionCN: 导致某人走向败亡的人或品质
senses.example: In the end, his own pride was his destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 最终，他自己的骄傲成了他的祸根。
senses.why: What destroys a person can be carried inside him all along.
senses.whyCN: 毁掉一个人的东西，可能一直就装在他自己身上。

intro.en: Destruction is Latin destructio, from destruere, to unbuild, built on de- and struere, to pile up.
intro.cn: destruction 是拉丁语 destructio，源于 destruere（拆建），由 de- 与 struere（堆起）构成。

items.en: Destructio named the pulling down of a structure.
items.cn: destructio 指把一座建筑拉倒。

items.en: It also covered the ruin of a city, a plan or a life.
items.cn: 它同样涵盖城市、计划或人生的毁败。

items.en: French destruccion kept the double weight of act and result.
items.cn: 法语 destruccion 保留了行为与结果的双重分量。

items.en: English used it for wars, fires and moral ruin alike.
items.cn: 英语把它同样用于战争、火灾与道德上的败亡。

items.en: Modern usage adds the slow destruction of forests and climate.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上了森林与气候那种缓慢的破坏。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in -struction or -struction-like shapes, and the meaning group all name serious damage.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -struction 一类的形状收尾，近义组则都指严重的损坏。

entries.definition: the work of building something
entries.definitionCN: 建造某物的工程

entries.definition: information telling you how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 说明如何做某事的信息

entries.definition: something that blocks the way
entries.definitionCN: 挡住去路的东西

entries.definition: the state of being spoiled or lost
entries.definitionCN: 被毁坏或失去的状态

entries.definition: great damage over a wide area
entries.definitionCN: 大范围内的大规模损害

entries.definition: harm done to something
entries.definitionCN: 对某物造成的损害

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a roof open to the sky and end with a man undone by his own pride.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一顶对着天空敞开的屋顶开始，落到一个被自己骄傲毁掉的人。

normal.en: Construction and destruction differ by one small prefix.
normal.cn: 建造与毁坏，只差一个小前缀。

normal.en: The noun keeps what the verb has already finished.
normal.cn: 动词做完的事，名词把它留在原地。

normal.en: A storm leaves destruction; a decision leaves it too.
normal.cn: 风暴留下破坏，一个决定同样会留下破坏。

normal.en: The word can describe a city, a forest or a single life.
normal.cn: 这个词能形容一座城、一片林，也能形容一个人的一生。

normal.en: What ruins a man may be the very thing he is proud of.
normal.cn: 毁掉一个人的，也许正是他最引以为傲的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a roof frame with nothing left above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一副屋顶的骨架，上面什么都没有了。

abstract.en: Picture a street covered in wet broken tiles.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街铺满湿透的碎瓦。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror cracked across the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一面从中间裂开的镜子。

examples.en: The storm left a wide trail of destruction.
examples.cn: 这场风暴留下了一大片破坏的痕迹。

examples.en: The destruction of the old bridge took two days.
examples.cn: 拆除那座旧桥花了两天。

examples.en: In the end, his own pride was his destruction.
examples.cn: 最终，他自己的骄傲成了他的祸根。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destruction 记成「地斯抓克神」：de 是去掉，struct 是建造，建造被去掉，就成了破坏。

root: 来自拉丁语 destructio，源于 destruere（拆掉建筑），由 de-（去掉）与 struere（堆起、建造）构成。本义是建筑被拉倒，后来指城市、计划与人生的毁败，现代又指森林与气候那种缓慢而大范围的破坏。

sensesIntro.en: From the wreck left after a force passes, to the deliberate tearing down, to the flaw inside a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从力量过后留下的残骸，到有意的拆除，再到一个人心里的那处缺口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure standing open to the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座向天空敞开的建筑残骸。

branches.en: The first sense is the wreck as it lies there afterward.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是事后躺在那里的残骸。

branches.en: The second sense is the work of pulling it down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把它拉倒的那份劳作。

branches.en: The third sense is a ruin that comes from inside.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是从内部生出的毁败。

branches.en: A noun can hold both the deed and the debris.
branches.cn: 一个名词可以同时装着行为与废堆。

branches.en: Storms ruin towns, and pride ruins the man who owns it.
branches.cn: 风暴毁掉城镇，骄傲毁掉拥有它的人。

intro.en: Destruction grows words for the quality, the manner and the impossibility of being destroyed.
intro.cn: destruction 长出表示性质、方式以及「无法被毁」的一族词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin struere, to build, and de- turns the building around; -tion makes the act a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 struere（建造），de- 把建造掉转方向，-tion 把动作变成名词。

items.meaning: the act or result of destroying
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了巨大破坏。
这些甲虫破坏性地蔓延。
他们测量了这场风暴的破坏力。

items.meaning: one who destroys, or a warship
items.exampleCN: 那艘驱逐舰离开了港口。

items.example: The town was destroyed in a night.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子一夜之间被毁。
这个箱子好像怎么都弄不坏。

definition_zh: 偶尔；有时；间或
definition_en: sometimes, but not often, and without a regular pattern
core_image: 一本日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白
scene: 老式收音机会在深夜突然冒出杂音。 The old radio occasionally crackles late at night.
sceneCN: 这里指不规律地偶尔发生（第 3 个义项：以不规则间隔出现）；句意为这台旧收音机深夜偶尔会噼啪作响；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Sometimes but not often
senses.definition: at times, with long gaps between occurrences
senses.definitionCN: 有时发生，但两次之间间隔较长
senses.example: I occasionally walk to work when the weather is fine.
senses.exampleCN: 天气好的时候，我偶尔步行去上班。
senses.why: The adverb sits on the lower part of the frequency scale, below sometimes and well below often.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词处在频率刻度的较低位置，低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frequency frame
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, setting a sporadic pattern
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为整句设定「零星发生」的模式
senses.example: Occasionally, the system fails without any warning.
senses.exampleCN: 偶尔，系统会在毫无预警的情况下失灵。
senses.why: The front position frames the whole event as an exception to the normal case.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个事件框成正常情形之外的例外。

senses.title: At irregular intervals
senses.definition: happening without a fixed schedule or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定时间表或规律地发生
senses.example: The machine occasionally jams during heavy use.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器在高负荷使用时会偶尔卡住。
senses.why: The word denies regularity: the events happen, but no rhythm can be predicted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否认规律性：事情会发生，却预测不出节奏。

senses.title: Now and then in speech
senses.definition: used in relaxed speech for an activity done from time to time
senses.definitionCN: 在轻松口语中指不时做一次的活动
senses.example: We occasionally meet for coffee after work.
senses.exampleCN: 我们下班后偶尔一起喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: The conversational register makes the word a soft way to describe a loose habit.
senses.whyCN: 口语语域让这个词成为描述松散习惯的柔和说法。

senses.title: Sporadic in technical writing
senses.definition: of faults or events that appear intermittently under certain conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指故障或事件在特定条件下间歇出现
senses.example: Errors occur occasionally when the load exceeds the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 当负载超过上限时，错误会偶尔出现。
senses.why: Technical reports use the word to admit a fault without claiming it is constant or reproducible.
senses.whyCN: 技术报告用它承认故障存在，却不声称它持续不断或可稳定复现。

senses.title: Deliberate understatement
senses.definition: used to make a frequent habit sound rarer than it is
senses.definitionCN: 用来把频繁的习惯说得比实际更稀少
senses.example: He occasionally drinks more than he should.
senses.exampleCN: 他偶尔会喝得超过应有的量。
senses.why: The choice of a low-frequency word can soften a description that the facts would support more strongly.
senses.whyCN: 选用低频率的词可以软化描述，而事实本可支持更强的说法。

senses.title: As an exception
senses.definition: used of a case that departs from the usual rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于偏离通常规则的情形
senses.example: Permission is occasionally granted for late applications.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申请偶尔会获得许可。
senses.why: The word marks the exception that proves the rule, keeping the general statement intact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出「证明规则」的例外，从而保住一般性说法。

senses.title: In older formal prose
senses.definition: in literary or dated writing, a refined substitute for sometimes
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或旧式文字中，作为「有时」的雅致替代
senses.example: The lake is occasionally visited by migrating birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湖泊间或有候鸟造访。
senses.why: The formal written use sounds more measured than sometimes and often appears in descriptive prose.
senses.whyCN: 正式书面用法比「有时」更有分寸，常见于描写性散文。

intro.en: Occasionally comes from the Latin verb for falling down or happening, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「落下、发生」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb cadere means to fall, as in a falling event.
items.cn: 动词意为「落下」，如事件降临。

items.en: The prefix ob-, meaning towards or upon, plus cadere gives occidere, to fall upon or set.
items.cn: 表示「朝向、落在」的前缀与「落下」合成「落到……上、沉降」。

items.en: The noun occasio names a chance that falls at one's feet, hence an occasion or opportunity.
items.cn: 名词指落到脚边的机会，也就是时机、场合。

items.en: English occasion comes through French and gives the adjective occasional, meaning happening now and then.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入「场合」，并派生形容词，意为「偶尔发生的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage places the adverb below sometimes on the scale of frequency.
items.cn: 现代用法把它排在频率刻度上低于「有时」的位置。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin falling-root, including a look-alike from a different root; the second group orders expressions of frequency.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「落下」词根，其中包括一个形近但不同源的词；第二组按频率排列近义说法。

entries.definition: A particular time or event; the noun behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的时刻或事件；副词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Happening from time to time; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不时发生的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: A philosophical view that events are caused directly by God on each occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 一种哲学观点，认为每次事件都由神直接引起。

entries.definition: Western; built on the Latin word for sunset, not on occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 西方的；由拉丁语「日落」构成，与「场合」无关。

entries.definition: On some occasions, more often than occasionally.
entries.definitionCN: 在某些场合，频率高于「偶尔」。

entries.definition: At intervals, without a fixed schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 间隔地，没有固定时间表。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for an irregular low frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示不规律的低频率。

entries.definition: In scattered, unpredictable instances.
entries.definitionCN: 以零散、不可预测的零星方式。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again, often of a physical process.
entries.definitionCN: 断断续续地，多用于物理过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real falling-root and the real position of the word on the frequency scale.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「落下」词根，以及这个词在频率刻度上的真实位置。

normal.en: The root means to fall, so the event drops in now and then rather than on schedule.
normal.cn: 词根意为「落下」，所以事件是不定时掉进来，而不是按日程来。

normal.en: It sits below sometimes and far below often on the ladder of frequency.
normal.cn: 在频率阶梯上，它低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

normal.en: Said first, it warns the listener that the next event is an exception.
normal.cn: 放在句首，它提醒听者接下来的事件只是例外。

normal.en: In a technical report it keeps a fault real without making it constant.
normal.cn: 在技术报告里，它让故障真实存在，却不把它说成持续不断。

normal.en: Used of a habit, it can politely make the habit sound rarer than it is.
normal.cn: 用于习惯时，它可以礼貌地把习惯说得比实际更稀少。

abstract.en: Occasionally is the word for the pattern that has no pattern.
abstract.cn: 「偶尔」是给「没有规律」的规律准备的词。

abstract.en: A low-frequency word is a dimmer switch for how much the listener should worry.
abstract.cn: 低频词像一个调光开关，控制听者该担心多少。

abstract.en: The exception needs a name so that the rule can stay standing.
abstract.cn: 例外需要一个名字，规则才能继续站着。

examples.en: The system occasionally restarts on its own.
examples.cn: 系统偶尔会自行重启。

examples.en: Occasionally, the lake freezes over completely.
examples.cn: 偶尔，湖面会完全封冻。

examples.en: She occasionally writes to the local paper.
examples.cn: 她偶尔给当地报纸投稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「偶开胜利」——偶尔才开一次，不是常常

root: 拉丁语动词「落下」加表示「朝向」的前缀构成「落到……上、发生」，名词指落到脚边的时机；英语经法语借入名词并派生形容词「偶尔的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate low frequency, the sentence-opening frame, irregular intervals, relaxed speech, technical sporadicity, deliberate understatement, exception marking and older formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理低频、句首框架、不规则间隔、轻松口语、技术上的偶发、有意轻描淡写、标出例外，以及旧式书面用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with a few small circles and mostly empty days.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白。

branches.en: THE LOW RATE: less often than sometimes.
branches.cn: 低频率：比「有时」更少。

branches.en: THE UNEVEN PATTERN: the opening frame and the irregular interval.
branches.cn: 不均匀的模式：句首框架与不规则间隔。

branches.en: THE SOFT HABIT: the relaxed spoken way to describe a loose routine.
branches.cn: 柔和的习惯：口语中描述松散日常的方式。

branches.en: THE MANAGED CLAIM: technical sporadicity and deliberate understatement.
branches.cn: 被管理的说法：技术上的偶发与有意的轻描淡写。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: a departure from the rule, and the older formal tone.
branches.cn: 例外：对规则的偏离，以及较旧的正式语气。

intro.en: Occasionally is a Latin towards-prefix, a falling-root, a noun of occasion, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「朝向」前缀、「落下」词根、表「时机」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere is about falling; the prefixed verb names what falls upon a person, and the noun turns that into an occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「落下」；加前缀的动词指落到某人身上的事，名词再把它变成「时机」。

items.example: The prefix points the falling toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「落下」指向某人。

items.example: The verb gives the family its image of an event arriving.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「事件降临」的意象。

items.example: The compound verb covers both happening and the setting sun.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词既指「发生」，也指「日落」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表「发生之事」的名词。

items.example: The noun names the chance that happens to arrive.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指恰好到来的机会。

items.example: English borrows the noun through French.
items.exampleCN: 英语经法语借入这个名词。

items.example: The adjective shifts the noun from an event to a frequency.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把名词从「事件」转向「频率」。

items.example: The philosophical noun keeps the idea of events falling on each occasion.
items.exampleCN: 这一哲学名词保留「每次场合事件降临」的观念。

items.example: The suffix turns occasional into a frequency adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成频率副词。

definition_zh: 武器；兵器；手段（斗争或取胜的凭借）
definition_en: an object used to hurt or defeat an opponent, and also any method used to win a struggle
core_image: 一把长矛斜靠在石墙上，矛尖还有磨过的亮痕
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里，一支锈迹斑斑的长矛横放在绒布上，旁边标签写着它的出土年代。 The spear in the case was the first weapon found at the site.
sceneCN: 这里 weapon 是「武器」（第 1 个义项：用来伤害或战胜对手的器具）；句意为柜中这支长矛是遗址出土的第一件武器。斜靠石墙、矛尖带亮痕的长矛就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: An object made to hurt
senses.definition: a tool or device designed to injure, kill or defeat an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 为伤害、杀死或击败对手而设计的器具
senses.example: The soldiers laid down their weapons at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时放下武器。
senses.why: This is the physical core: a made thing with a harmful purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：一件有伤害用途的制成品。

senses.title: Armed force in general
senses.definition: armed strength seen as a whole, as in a balance of weapons
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的武装力量，如武器平衡
senses.example: Talks on limiting weapons resumed last week.
senses.exampleCN: 限制军备的会谈上周恢复。
senses.why: One object becomes a class of objects and then a form of power.
senses.whyCN: 一件器物成为一类器物，再成为一种力量。

senses.title: A means of winning a struggle
senses.definition: anything used to gain an advantage in an argument, contest or campaign
senses.definitionCN: 在争论、竞争或运动中用来取得优势的任何东西
senses.example: Information is the most useful weapon in this campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 在这场竞选里，信息是最有用的武器。
senses.why: A contest is fought like a battle, so its best tool becomes a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 竞争也像打仗一样进行，于是最好的工具就成了武器。

senses.title: A way of fighting something harmful
senses.definition: a method used against a disease, a problem or a natural danger
senses.definitionCN: 用来对抗疾病、问题或自然危险的方法
senses.example: Vaccination is our best weapon against the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗是我们对抗这种疾病的最好手段。
senses.why: Even a fight against illness borrows the language of arms.
senses.whyCN: 连对抗疾病也借用了兵器的说法。

senses.title: Something one is skilled with
senses.definition: a skill or quality that gives its owner an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 给拥有者带来优势的技能或特质
senses.example: Her patience was a weapon in long negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的谈判中，她的耐心就是一件利器。
senses.why: A personal quality that wins ground is spoken of as if it were carried in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 能赢下一块地盘的个人品质，被说得像握在手中一样。

intro.en: Weapon comes from Old English wǣpen, a Germanic word of unknown deeper origin, and has meant an instrument of fighting for a thousand years.
intro.cn: weapon 来自古英语 wǣpen，是更早来源不明的日耳曼词，一千年来一直指打斗的器具。

items.en: The Germanic form wǣpnam named an implement of battle, and related words survive in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 wǣpnam 指战斗器具，荷兰语与德语中仍有相关词。

items.en: Wǣpen could mean a single weapon or arms in general, and appeared in heroic poetry.
items.cn: wǣpen 可指单件武器，也可泛指武装，见于英雄诗歌。

items.en: Spelling shifted towards weapon, and the plural weapons became the usual collective form.
items.cn: 拼写趋向 weapon，复数 weapons 成为常用集合形式。

items.en: Gunpowder gave the word a second life in phrases such as nuclear weapons.
items.cn: 火药与核技术让这个词在 nuclear weapons 等说法中获得第二次生命。

items.en: The figurative use, a weapon against poverty, is now entirely standard.
items.cn: 比喻用法「对抗贫困的武器」如今已完全标准。

note.en: The first group is built on the weapon word itself, the second are the other names for arms.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 weapon 这个词上，第二组是武器的其他说法。

entries.definition: Weapons as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 武器（总称）

entries.definition: To turn something into a weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 使武器化

entries.definition: Without any weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 无武器的

entries.definition: To arm again.
entries.definitionCN: 重新武装

entries.definition: Weapons used in war, plural in form.
entries.definitionCN: 武器；军械

entries.definition: A weapon that fires a projectile.
entries.definitionCN: 枪；炮

entries.definition: An implement used to do work, neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 工具

entries.definition: The method used to reach an end.
entries.definitionCN: 手段；方法

normalIntro.en: Keep the physical weapon in view, then let it travel into arguments and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 先盯住实物武器，再看它走进争论与医学。

normal.en: Weapon is the singular; arms is the plural collective.
normal.cn: weapon 是单数，arms 是复数集合。

normal.en: Weaponry is the mass noun for weapons as a whole.
normal.cn: weaponry 作为物质名词指全部武器。

normal.en: Weaponize means to make a weapon of something.
normal.cn: weaponize 是把某物做成武器。

normal.en: A weapon against a disease is a cure, not a gun.
normal.cn: a weapon against a disease 是疗法，不是枪。

normal.en: Information as a weapon is the commonest figurative use.
normal.cn: 信息作为武器是最常见的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture a spear leaning on cold stone.
abstract.cn: 想一支矛斜靠在冰冷的石上。

abstract.en: Feel the balance of a long shaft in one hand.
abstract.cn: 感受一只手握长杆时的重量平衡。

abstract.en: See a sign that says the spear was the first of its kind here.
abstract.cn: 看一块牌子写着这是此地出土的第一件。

examples.en: The police found a weapon in the car.
examples.cn: 警察在车里发现了一件武器。

examples.en: Education is a powerful weapon against poverty.
examples.cn: 教育是对抗贫困的有力武器。

examples.en: They accused each other of using gossip as a weapon.
examples.cn: 他们互相指责对方把流言当武器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威朋」——威朋把长矛靠在门口，说这是护家的第一件武器。

root: 日耳曼语 wǣpnam（战斗器具）→ 古英语 wǣpen → 中古英语 weapon；同源词有 weaponry、weaponize。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as one made object, widens to armed force, then turns to any means of winning or fighting.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一件制成品出发，扩大到武装力量，再转向任何取胜或对抗的手段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spear leaning against a stone wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支斜靠石墙的长矛。

branches.en: The object branch: weapons laid down at dawn.
branches.cn: 器物分支：黎明时放下的武器。

branches.en: The collective branch: talks on limiting weapons.
branches.cn: 集合分支：限制军备的会谈。

branches.en: The means branch: information in a campaign, a vaccine against illness.
branches.cn: 手段分支：竞选中的信息，对抗疾病的疫苗。

branches.en: The personal branch: patience as a negotiator’s weapon.
branches.cn: 个人分支：谈判者的耐心。

branches.en: The origin branch: an object held in the hand.
branches.cn: 起源分支：握在手中的器物。

intro.en: Weapon takes the ordinary noun and verb endings of English, chiefly in modern coinages.
intro.cn: weapon 采用英语常见的名词与动词词尾，主要用于现代新造词。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin source, so the Latin table stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 大头针；别针；销钉；插脚；别住；钉住；固定
definition_en: a small pointed metal fastener, or a part of a machine or plug, or to fasten something with such a pin
core_image: 一枚又细又尖的小金属针，把两样东西死死别在一起
scene: 她把写着座位的纸条别在校服领口，怕自己又忘了教室。 She used a pin to fix the note to her collar.
sceneCN: 这里是「别住」（第 5 个义项：用别针把东西固定）；句意是她用别针把纸条固定在领口。画面里就是那枚把纸条按在布上的小针。

derivatives.zh: pin 加 -ing 构成，义为「钉固；固定」
与拉丁钳形词相关，义为「钳子；钳形运动」
pin 与 head 复合，义为「针头；极小的东西」
pin 与 point 复合，义为「精确定位」

senses.title: A small pointed metal fastener
senses.definition: a thin pointed piece of metal with a head, used to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 带针头的细尖金属，用来把东西固定在一起
senses.example: The tailor held the fold in place with a pin.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝用一枚别针把褶子固定住。
senses.why: Latin pinna meant a feather, then a pointed quill, then anything sharp and thin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pinna 指羽毛，继而指羽茎，再引申为任何尖细之物。

senses.title: A pin as a safety fastener
senses.definition: a pin with a coiled spring and a protective cover over the point
senses.definitionCN: 带弹簧圈和护针帽的别针
senses.example: A safety pin held the torn strap.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚安全别针别住了撕破的带子。
senses.why: The invention adds protection to the naked point of the pin.
senses.whyCN: 这项发明给裸露的针尖加了保护。

senses.title: A machine or plug pin
senses.definition: a small metal rod that holds machine parts together or connects a plug
senses.definitionCN: 固定机器部件或连接插头的小金属杆
senses.example: One bent pin stopped the plug from fitting.
senses.exampleCN: 一根弯了的插脚让插头插不进去。
senses.why: The sharp slender shape transfers from cloth to machinery.
senses.whyCN: 尖细的形状从布料转移到机械上。

senses.title: A personal identification code
senses.definition: a secret number used with a bank card or device
senses.definitionCN: 配合银行卡或设备使用的保密数字
senses.example: She changed her bank pin after the phone was stolen.
senses.exampleCN: 手机被盗后她改了银行卡密码。
senses.why: The acronym PIN was later spelled like the word, and the meanings fused.
senses.whyCN: 缩写 PIN 后来拼成与该词相同，两义融合。

senses.title: To fasten with a pin
senses.definition: to attach something using a pin or similar pointed object
senses.definitionCN: 用别针或类似尖物把东西固定
senses.example: He pinned the medal onto his jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把勋章别在夹克上。
senses.why: The tool gives its name to the act done with it.
senses.whyCN: 工具把自己的名字给了用它完成的动作。

senses.title: To hold someone down
senses.definition: to press a person or animal so they cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 压制人或动物使之无法动弹
senses.example: The wrestler pinned his opponent to the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 摔跤手把对手按在垫子上。
senses.why: The needle fixes cloth; the same fixing force fixes a body.
senses.whyCN: 针固定布料；同样的固定之力固定身体。

senses.title: To identify precisely
senses.definition: to establish a fact, cause or position exactly
senses.definitionCN: 准确查明事实、原因或位置
senses.example: Doctors finally pinned down the cause of the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生终于查明了疼痛的原因。
senses.why: A pin marks one exact point; the idiom transfers that to facts.
senses.whyCN: 针标记一个精确点；习语把这一点转移到事实。

intro.en: Pin comes from Latin pinna or penna, a feather, whose quill stem gave the sense of a pointed shaft; Middle English took the word from Old French.
intro.cn: pin 源自拉丁语 pinna 或 penna（羽毛），其羽茎之义给出尖杆之感；中古英语经古法语得到该词。

items.en: Pinna meant feather, fin or a pointed projecting part.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 指羽毛、鳍或尖出的部分。

items.en: The pointed-stem sense produced pinna as a sharp fastening in late usage.
items.cn: 晚期用法中尖茎之义使 pinna 指尖状固定物。

items.en: Frenchpine and related forms passed the little spike into Norman speech.
items.cn: 法语相关形式把小尖钉传入诺曼语。

items.en: Pin named the sewing needle-like fastener from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 十三世纪起 pin 指类似缝针的固定器。

items.en: Engineering pins, plug pins and the digital PIN code kept the small sharp shape alive.
items.cn: 工程销钉、插脚和数字 PIN 码延续了小而尖的形象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pointed Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers fasteners and fixing words.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁尖物词族；近义组收固定件与固定用语。

entries.definition: The exact point of a pin, then very precise identification.
entries.definitionCN: 针尖点，进而指极精确的定位。

entries.definition: The head of a pin, and anything absurdly tiny.
entries.definitionCN: 针头，以及小得可笑的东西。

entries.definition: A small wing or peak, now the highest point of success.
entries.definitionCN: 原指小尖顶，现指成功的顶点。

entries.definition: A sharp fastener driven by a hammer, larger and rougher.
entries.definitionCN: 用锤敲入的尖钉，更大更粗。

entries.definition: A short flat-headed nail for pinning papers.
entries.definitionCN: 平头小钉，用于钉纸。

entries.definition: A device that grips without piercing.
entries.definitionCN: 夹住而不刺穿的东西。

normalIntro.en: The whole family descends from a feather: thin, pointed, and able to hold two things together.
normalIntro.cn: 整个词族都出自羽毛：细、尖、能把两样东西别在一起。

normal.en: Latin pinna, feather — a quill was nature's first pin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 是羽毛——翎管是大自然的第一枚别针。

normal.en: Pin down does double duty: hold a body still or fix a fact.
normal.cn: pin down 一语双用：按住身体或锁定事实。

normal.en: The pin on a plug and the pin on a badge share one slim metal body.
normal.cn: 插头上的插脚和徽章上的别针共用同一根细金属。

normal.en: PIN codes borrowed the spelling and gave the old word a digital life.
normal.cn: PIN 码借用了拼写，给老词以数字生命。

normal.en: Pinned hopes hang their whole weight on one slim point.
normal.cn: pinned hopes 把全部重量挂在细小的一点上。

abstract.en: One point of contact: the pin holds the world together at its thinnest.
abstract.cn: 一个接触点：别针以最细处撑住世界。

abstract.en: Being pinned is the opposite of freedom — a body, a plan, a blame.
abstract.cn: 被钉住是自由的反面——身体、计划、罪名皆然。

abstract.en: From quill to code, the pin keeps puncturing new meanings.
abstract.cn: 从翎管到代码，别针不断刺出新义。

examples.en: She pinned a rose to his lapel.
examples.cn: 她把一朵玫瑰别在他的翻领上。

examples.en: Rescuers pinned the blame on faulty wiring.
examples.cn: 调查者把责任定位于线路故障。

examples.en: The car pinned his leg against the wall.
examples.cn: 汽车把他的腿抵在了墙上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼」——把两张纸拼在一起，靠的就是一根小针；pin 就是别针。

root: 拉丁语 pinna / penna（羽毛、羽茎、尖突）经古法语进入中古英语成为 pin；羽毛的细尖形态是所有义项的核心。

sensesIntro.en: One thin point runs from the sewing box through machinery, wrestling mats and bank security to precise identification.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根细尖从针线盒贯穿机械、摔跤垫、银行安全，直至精确定位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp thin point that joins or fixes what it pierces.
core.cn: 核心意象：细而尖的一点，刺入并固定它所穿透之物。

branches.en: a fold of cloth held still
branches.cn: 被固定不动的布褶

branches.en: a medal placed on a jacket
branches.cn: 别上夹克的勋章

branches.en: shoulders pressed to a mat
branches.cn: 被按在垫子上的肩膀

branches.en: a doctor circling the true cause
branches.cn: 圈出真正病因的医生

branches.en: the same slim rod in a socket and in a code
branches.cn: 同一根细杆：在插座里，也在密码中

intro.en: Pin builds compounds eagerly, from pinhead to pinball, all preserving the small sharp image.
intro.cn: pin 乐于构成复合词，从针头到弹球机，都保留小而尖的形象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin feather root also gave pen and pinnacle, its most famous relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁羽毛词根还派生了 pen 和 pinnacle 这两位最著名的亲戚。

derivatives.zh: 复合词，义为「针头；极小之物」

definition_zh: 议会；国会；（英国的）议会；（一届全国议会的）任期
definition_en: the national lawmaking assembly of a country, especially one in which the government is drawn from its members
core_image: 一间圆形大厅里两排长凳相对而坐，中间的地毯上放着一份待辩的文件
scene: 圆形大厅里两排长凳相对，中间的地毯上摊着一份文件。 Parliament debated the bill until midnight.
sceneCN: 句中这个词指一国的国家立法议会，尤其指政府由议员产生的体制（第 1 个义项：由民选代表组成、掌握立法权的国家议会）；句意为议会辩论该法案直到午夜。图中可辨识物件：两排长凳、中央地毯、文件、议长席位、表决通道；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 一届议会的任期；议会会议时期

senses.title: A national lawmaking assembly
senses.definition: the supreme lawmaking body of a state, especially where the executive answers to it
senses.definitionCN: 一国的最高立法机构，尤指行政须向它负责的体制
senses.example: Parliament debated the bill until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 议会辩论该法案直到午夜。
senses.why: The word first meant a talking together, and the national assembly is the place where the talking decides law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「一起说话」，而国家议会就是说话决定法律的地方。

senses.title: The building
senses.definition: the building or chamber where the assembly meets
senses.definitionCN: 议会开会所在的建筑或议事厅
senses.example: A crowd gathered outside parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 一群人聚集在议会大厦外。
senses.why: By metonymy the place takes the name of the body that meets in it.
senses.whyCN: 借代作用使地点取得了在其中开会之机构的名字。

senses.title: The members collectively
senses.definition: the assembled members considered as one actor
senses.definitionCN: 把全体议员视为一个行动者
senses.example: Parliament was divided on the question.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在这个问题上意见分裂。
senses.why: A body acts through votes, so the name passes from the institution to the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 机构通过投票行动，于是名称从制度转到里面的人。

senses.title: A term or session
senses.definition: the period between one general election and the next, or a single session
senses.definitionCN: 两次大选之间的一段时期，或一次会期
senses.example: The law was passed in the last parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律在上一届议会任期内通过。
senses.why: Because the assembly is dissolved and reconstituted, the word also counts the periods of its life.
senses.whyCN: 由于议会被解散又重新组成，这个词也用来数它生命的周期。

senses.title: A medieval council
senses.titleCN: 中世纪由君主召集的会议
senses.definition: a conference of nobles and clergy summoned by a monarch to advise and consent
senses.definitionCN: 由君主召集、由贵族与教士提供建议并同意的会议
senses.example: The medieval parliament began as a royal council.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的议会起初是王室会议。
senses.why: Before it made law, the assembly was a speaking-together called by the king, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 在制定法律之前，这个集会是由国王召集的「一起说话」，那是最老的义项。

senses.title: A regional or supranational parliament
senses.definition: a lawmaking or deliberative assembly below or above the national level
senses.definitionCN: 低于或高于国家层级的立法或议事议会
senses.example: The Scottish Parliament sits in Edinburgh.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰议会设在爱丁堡。
senses.why: Once the model exists, it can be copied at any level, from a province to a continent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了这个模式，它就能被复制到任何层级，从一省到一洲。

senses.title: Any deliberative assembly
senses.definition: an extended use for a meeting that argues out a decision
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法，指通过争论作出决定的会议
senses.example: The students held a parliament on the library steps.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在图书馆台阶上开了一场议事会。
senses.why: Talking toward a decision is the original action, so the label travels to any group that does it.
senses.whyCN: 为了决定而说话是原本的动作，因此这个标签能转到任何这样做的群体。

senses.title: A literary gathering
senses.titleCN: 文学中的群鸟议事（典故）
senses.definition: the title word of medieval poems in which birds or beasts hold a council
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪诗题中的用词，写群鸟或群兽开会
senses.example: Chaucer's poem is known as the Parliament of Fowls.
senses.exampleCN: 乔叟那首诗被称为《百鸟议会》。
senses.why: The poem takes the assembly's name and applies it to birds, which is the word's most playful reach.
senses.whyCN: 这首诗借用了议会的名字，把它用在鸟身上，是这个词汇最俏皮的延伸。

intro.en: Parliament comes from Old French parlement, first 'a speaking, talk' and then 'a conference'. The verb parler 'to speak' goes back through Late Latin parabolare to parabola 'speech, comparison', from Greek parabole.
intro.cn: parliament 来自古法语 parlement，最初意为「说话、谈话」，后指「会议」。动词 parler「说话」经晚期拉丁 parabolare 上溯到 parabola「言语、比较」，再上溯到希腊语 parabole。

items.en: Parabole meant a placing beside, hence a comparison and a story used as a comparison. It passed into Latin as parabola.
items.cn: parabole 意为「放在旁边」，因此指比较，也指用作比较的故事。它进入拉丁语作 parabola。

items.en: The verb parabolare 'to speak, talk' grew out of parabola in late and vulgar Latin, and from it came French parler.
items.cn: 动词 parabolare「说话、谈话」在晚期与通俗拉丁语中由 parabola 长出，法语 parler 即由此而来。

items.en: Parlement named a speaking or a conference before it named an institution; the Anglo-Latin form parliamentum is recorded from the early thirteenth century.
items.cn: parlement 先指说话或会谈，后指机构；其盎格鲁拉丁形式 parliamentum 自十三世纪早期见于记录。

items.en: English parliament is recorded about 1300 for a formal conference, and by the mid-fourteenth century for the representative assembly of England.
items.cn: 英语 parliament 约在 1300 年指正式会议，到十四世纪中期指英格兰的代表性议会。

items.en: The spelling was altered about 1400 to match Medieval Latin parliamentum, which is why the word has an i that the French form lacks.
items.cn: 拼写约在 1400 年按中世纪拉丁 parliamentum 改动，这就是为什么这个词有一个法语形式所无的 i。

items.en: The chain from Greek parabole is clear. Only the earliest citation of each English sense is approximate, so no source is marked uncertain.
items.cn: 从希腊 parabole 以来的链条清楚。只有各英语义项的最早书证是约数，因此没有需要标为来源不确定的部分。

note.en: Group one holds words sharing the speaking root behind parliament; group two holds other assemblies that decide by debate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 parliament 背后「说话」词根的词；第二组是同样以辩论作决定的其他集会。

entries.definition: A conference with an enemy, from the same French verb; it is a talk, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指与敌方的会谈，出自同一个法语动词；它是一次谈话，不是机构。

entries.definition: A sitting room for conversation; the old sense of a room set apart for talking survives here.
entries.definitionCN: 指供谈话的起居室；「专门用于说话的房间」这一旧义在此留存。

entries.definition: A prisoner's promise of good behaviour, literally a word given; it comes through the same speaking root.
entries.definitionCN: 指囚犯作出的守规承诺，字面是「给出的话」；它经同一个「说话」词根而来。

entries.definition: A short story used to illustrate a moral point, directly from Greek parabole; parliament's root is a speaking verb grown from this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来说明道理的短故事，直接来自希腊 parabole；parliament 的词根是由这个名词长出的说话动词。

entries.definition: A national legislature, especially the American one; its image is people coming together, not people speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家立法机关，尤指美国国会；其意象是人走到一起，而非人说话。

entries.definition: The general term for a lawmaking body; parliament is the specific model in which the executive sits inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指立法机关的通用说法；parliament 是行政也坐在其中的特定模式。

entries.definition: Any gathering of people, including a lawmaking one; it is the broad noun that parliament narrows.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何人群聚集，包括立法性集会；它是 parliament 所收窄的宽泛名词。

entries.definition: The name of certain historical assemblies, as in the Diet of Worms; the word came from a day's appointed meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 指某些历史性议会的名称，如沃尔姆斯议会；这个词来自约定的会面日。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real speaking root, the real family and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「说话」词根、真实词族与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: parler 'to speak': the place where a country talks its laws into being.
normal.cn: parler「说话」：一个国家通过说话把法律谈出来的地方。

normal.en: The family runs parliament, parliamentary, parliamentarian, parley, parlour and parole.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 parliament、parliamentary、parliamentarian、parley、parlour 与 parole。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institution: member of parliament, dissolve parliament, a sitting of parliament.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机构用法：议会议员、解散议会、议会的一次会议。

normal.en: The i in the spelling was restored from Medieval Latin, not taken from French.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 i 是从中世纪拉丁语回补的，并非取自法语。

normal.en: The root is Greek parabole, which also gave parable and parabola.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊 parabole，它还给了 parable 与 parabola。

abstract.en: Picture two benches facing each other, with all the distance between them measured by a sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两条长凳相对，两人之间的距离用一张纸来丈量。

abstract.en: Picture a building that is empty half the year and loud the other half.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋建筑半年空着，另外半年很吵。

abstract.en: Picture a nest of birds arranged like a debating hall, each beak raised in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一窝鸟排成议事厅的样子，每只轮流举喙。

examples.en: Parliament rejected the treaty by a narrow majority.
examples.cn: 议会以微弱多数否决了该条约。

examples.en: She was elected to parliament at twenty-nine.
examples.cn: 她二十九岁当选议员。

examples.en: The old parliament building is now a museum.
examples.cn: 旧的议会大厦如今是博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕了-门特」——议员在「门特」（门口）里吵得让人「怕了」，但吵完还是要表决 → 议会

root: 古法语 parlement「说话、会谈」← parler「说话」← 晚期拉丁 parabolare ← 拉丁 parabola「言语、比较」← 希腊 parabole「放在旁边、比喻」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of talking: talk becomes a royal council, then a national assembly, then its building, its members, its term, its regional copies, any debating group and finally a poem about birds.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「说话」动作展开：说话先变成王室会议，再变成国家议会，然后是它的建筑、议员、任期、地区复制版、任何辩论团体，最后是一首写鸟的诗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two facing benches with a sheet of paper lying between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排相对的长凳，中间放着一页纸。

branches.en: FROM TALK TO LAW: a council summoned to speak becomes an assembly whose speaking makes law.
branches.cn: 从说话到法律：被召来说话的会议，变成说话即立法的议会。

branches.en: PLACE AND PERSONS: the building and the members both take the institution's name.
branches.cn: 地点与人：建筑与议员都取用了机构的名字。

branches.en: COUNTING TIME: a body that is dissolved and re-formed can be counted by its terms.
branches.cn: 数着时间：被解散又重新组成的机构，可以按任期来计数。

branches.en: COPIED SCALE: a province and a student rally both reuse the model of arguing toward a decision.
branches.cn: 复制的尺度：一个省与一场学生集会都复用了「争到决定」的模式。

branches.en: THE BIRDS: the most playful reach applies the assembly's name to a flock in a poem.
branches.cn: 群鸟：最俏皮的延伸把议会的名字用在诗中的一群鸟上。

intro.en: Parliament is a French noun from a Latin-speaking verb that itself grew from a Greek noun, so its family spans three languages.
intro.cn: parliament 是一个法语名词，出自一个拉丁「说话」动词，而该动词又由希腊名词长出，因此这个词族横跨三种语言。

latinIntro.en: Greek parabole gives Latin parabola, Late Latin parabolare and French parler, from which parliament, parley, parlour and parole all descend.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 parabole 给出拉丁 parabola、晚期拉丁 parabolare 与法语 parler，parliament、parley、parlour 与 parole 都由后者传下。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Latin parabola also gave the English parable.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 parabola 还给了英语 parable。

items.example: The verb passed into French as parler.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入法语作 parler。

items.example: The French noun first meant talk, not a chamber.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词最初指谈话，不指议院。

items.structure: parlement + spelling from Medieval Latin parliamentum

items.example: The bill cleared its parliamentary stages.
items.exampleCN: 该法案通过了各议会阶段。
这位议事专家熟悉每一条先例。

items.example: The two sides met for a parley.

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: The ending marks the outcome of speaking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记说话的结果。

latinEntries.structure: parabola, parabolae (f., first declension, from Greek)
parliamentum, parliamenti (n., second declension, Medieval Latin)
